The 556 shop garments showed no matches on 8050 because nobody had labelled them yet. When I added them to the pool, I only collected and cut out the photos. I also never generated the 8050 suggestions for them: those were built when the pool held only the first 287 garments. The review page then made it look worse by showing "no library silhouette fits" for garments that simply had no labels.

Fixed: - Suggestions: 8050 now has suggested matches for all 858 garments. - Review page: it says "not labelled yet" for unlabelled garments and "excluded" for excluded ones. Both have their own filter. - Labels: I labelled all 556 shop garments the same way as before. I looked at each one next to its 15 suggested drawings and picked 1 to 3 best first, 2.4 on average. Every id is checked against the library, and your earlier labels are untouched. This is committed.

8050 now:

Garments
Clean, with matches 671
Bad cut-out (torn, cropped, a model in the photo, or a bra shot instead of the top) 149
Nothing in the library fits 23
Excluded (turtlenecks, a bomber jacket, one with a person in it) 15
Not labelled 0

The 23 "none fit" are mostly cardigans and sweaters, including knit polos and a cardigan sold as a "halter top". Your outerwear drawings in silhouettes/new/ will give them matches. I've recorded in DECISIONS.md that cardigans and sweaters go in outerwear.

One thing to know: the top × bottom pair scoring doesn't cover outerwear yet. Once cardigans and sweaters are in the library, they'll need their own pair ratings or rules.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Train the garment -> silhouette matcher and report how well it finds the right silhouettes.

4	Usage: ../embeddings/.venv/bin/python -I train.py [--labels] [--save head.npz]

6	(softmax inside the garment's slot). Trained on synthetic cloth renders of the drawings (synth.py); with --labels, also on the real
7	garments you labelled in the labeling screen (labels.jsonl; weighted up, since they are the real thing).
8	Reports (all rank-based, as several silhouettes can be right for one garment):
9	  synthetic validation  cloth textures never seen in training: top-1 / top-5 of the drawing the render came from
10	  real garments         your labelled picks (cross-validated: a garment is scored by a model that never saw it), or, before any
11	                        labels, the 25 hand-marked test garments: share where any right answer is in the top 1 / 3 / 5, mean reciprocal rank
12	Compared against: outline distance only, and CLIP zero-shot (garment vs the average embedding of each silhouette's renders).

34	
35	    def logits(self, f):
36	        x = torch.tensor(((np.atleast_2d(f) - self.mu) / self.sd).astype(np.float32))
37	        with torch.no_grad():
38	            return self.net(x).numpy()[0] if x.shape[0] == 1 else self.net(x).numpy()
39

41	def make_net(d, n, hidden=256):
42	    return torch.nn.Sequential(torch.nn.Linear(d, hidden), torch.nn.GELU(), torch.nn.Dropout(0.3), torch.nn.Linear(hidden, n))
43

45	def fit(X, Y, W, epochs=60, seed=0):
46	    """X features, Y soft targets (n, 220), W sample weights."""
47	    torch.manual_seed(seed)
48	    mu, sd = X.mean(0), X.std(0) + 1e-6
49	    x = torch.tensor(((X - mu) / sd).astype(np.float32))
50	    y, w = torch.tensor(Y.astype(np.float32)), torch.tensor(W.astype(np.float32))
51	    net = make_net(X.shape[1], Y.shape[1])
52	    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(net.parameters(), 2e-3, weight_decay=1e-2)
53	    n = len(x)
54	    for ep in range(epochs):
55	        net.train()
56	        perm = torch.randperm(n)
57	        for s in range(0, n, 256):
58	            b = perm[s:s + 256]
59	            xb = x[b] + 0.05 * torch.randn_like(x[b])  # feature noise: cloth the renders did not cover
60	            loss = (-(y[b] * Fn.log_softmax(net(xb), -1)).sum(-1) * w[b]).mean()
61	            opt.zero_grad(); loss.backward(); opt.step()
62	    net.eval()
63	    return Head(net, mu, sd)

69	    net.load_state_dict({k[2:]: torch.tensor(z[k]) for k in z.files if k.startswith("w_")})
70	    net.eval()

2	
3	    Extractor().features(img, mask)  -> 1-D float32 vector [512 CLIP | 24 profile | aspect, w_top, w_mid, w_low, taper, fill]
4	Usage (cache the training features):  ../embeddings/.venv/bin/python -I features.py [--per-class 30 --val-per-class 6]
5	"""
6	import argparse, json, random, sys, time
7	from pathlib import Path
8	
9	import numpy as np
10	import torch
11	from PIL import Image
12	
13	HERE = Path(__file__).parent
14	ROOT = HERE.parents[1]

17	from sil_tools import outline_profile  # noqa: E402
18

20	CLIP_DIM, OUT_DIM = 512, 512 + 24 + 6

22	
23	class Extractor:
24	    def __init__(self):
25	        import open_clip
26	        self.model, _, self.pre = open_clip.create_model_and_transforms("ViT-B-32", pretrained="laion2b_s34b_b79k")
27	        self.model.eval()
28	        self.dev = "mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu"
29	        self.model.to(self.dev)
30	
31	    @staticmethod
32	    def square(img):
33	        s = max(img.size)
34	        c = Image.new("RGB", (s, s), (255, 255, 255))
35	        c.paste(img.convert("RGB"), ((s - img.width) // 2, (s - img.height) // 2))
36	        return c
37	
38	    @staticmethod
39	    def shape(mask):
40	        p = outline_profile(mask)
41	        return np.array(p["profile"] + [p["aspect"], p["w_top"], p["w_mid"], p["w_low"], min(p["taper"], 5.0), p["fill"]], np.float32)
42	
43	    def clip(self, imgs, batch=64):
44	        out = []
45	        with torch.no_grad():
46	            for s in range(0, len(imgs), batch):
47	                x = torch.stack([self.pre(self.square(i)) for i in imgs[s:s + batch]]).to(self.dev)
48	                f = self.model.encode_image(x)
49	                out.append((f / f.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True)).cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32))
50	        return np.concatenate(out)
51	
52	    def features(self, imgs, masks):
53	        return np.concatenate([self.clip(imgs), np.stack([self.shape(m) for m in masks])], 1)
54	
55	
56	if __name__ == "__main__":
57	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
58	    ap.add_argument("--per-class", type=int, default=30)
59	    ap.add_argument("--val-per-class", type=int, default=6)
60	    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
61	    a = ap.parse_args()

79	        np.savez_compressed(OUT / f"synth_{split}.npz", X=np.concatenate(X), y=np.array(y), ids=np.array(ids))

20	export function srgbToLab([r, g, b]: number[]): [number, number, number] {
21	  const lin = [r, g, b].map((v) => {
22	    const c = v / 255;
23	    return c <= 0.04045 ? c / 12.92 : ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4;
24	  });
25	  const [x, y, z] = [

28	    (0.0193 * lin[0] + 0.1192 * lin[1] + 0.9505 * lin[2]) / 1.08883,
29	  ];
30	  const f = (t: number) => (t > 216 / 24389 ? Math.cbrt(t) : ((24389 / 27) * t + 16) / 116);
31	  return [116 * f(y) - 16, 500 * (f(x) - f(y)), 200 * (f(y) - f(z))];

39	  const w = Math.min(C / 20, 1);

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Rank every silhouette of the right slot for each pooled garment, so the labeling screen can show the likeliest ones first.
3	
4	Usage: ../embeddings/.venv/bin/python -I candidates.py [--model head.npz]
5	Before any labels exist the ranking is zero-shot: how close the garment's CLIP embedding is to the average embedding of the
6	silhouette's photo-like renders, minus how far its outline is from the silhouette's outline (both as z-scores inside the slot).
7	Once a trained head exists (train.py) pass --model and its scores are used instead (plus the same outline term).
8	Writes datasets/silhouette-match/candidates.json: {garment id: [[silhouette id, score], ...] best first}.
9	"""
10	import argparse, json, sys
11	from pathlib import Path
12	
13	import numpy as np
14	from PIL import Image
15	
16	HERE = Path(__file__).parent
17	ROOT = HERE.parents[1]
18	sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
19	from features import CLIP_DIM, OUT, Extractor  # noqa: E402
20	
21	ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
22	ap.add_argument("--model", default=None)
23	args = ap.parse_args()
24	lib = json.load(open(ROOT / "src/lib/styling/silhouettes.json"))
25	ids = [e["id"] for e in lib]
26	slot = np.array([e["slot"] for e in lib])
27	tr = np.load(OUT / "synth_train.npz")
28	cent = np.stack([tr["X"][tr["y"] == c, :CLIP_DIM].mean(0) for c in range(len(ids))])
29	cent /= np.linalg.norm(cent, axis=1, keepdims=True)
30	shape_lib = np.stack([tr["X"][tr["y"] == c, CLIP_DIM:].mean(0) for c in range(len(ids))])
31	pool = json.load(open(OUT / "pool/pool.json"))
32	ex = Extractor()
33	imgs = [Image.open(OUT / "pool" / f"{p['id']}_cut.png") for p in pool]
34	masks = [np.asarray(Image.open(OUT / "pool" / f"{p['id']}_mask.png")) > 127 for p in pool]
35	F = ex.features(imgs, masks)
36	np.savez(OUT / "pool_features.npz", X=F, ids=np.array([p["id"] for p in pool]))
37	z = lambda a: (a - a.mean()) / (a.std() + 1e-9)
38	head = None
39	if args.model:
40	    from train import Head, load_head  # noqa: E402
41	    head = load_head(args.model)
42	res = {}
43	for f, p in zip(F, pool):
44	    idx = np.nonzero(slot == p["slot"])[0]
45	    sim = (cent[idx] @ f[:CLIP_DIM]) if head is None else head.logits(f)[idx]
46	    d = np.abs(shape_lib[idx, :24] - f[CLIP_DIM:CLIP_DIM + 24]).mean(1) + 0.15 * np.abs(shape_lib[idx, 24] - f[CLIP_DIM + 24])
47	    s = z(sim) - z(d)
48	    order = np.argsort(-s)
49	    res[p["id"]] = [[ids[idx[i]], round(float(s[i]), 3)] for i in order]
50	json.dump(res, open(OUT / "candidates.json", "w"))
51	print(len(res), "garments ranked")
52

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Train and evaluate the silhouette-pair rating model on the rater's ratings.
3	
4	Usage: ../embeddings/.venv/bin/python -I train.py [--data ../../datasets/silhouettepairs] [--log]
5	
6	Per silhouette the input is measured, not a name: outline profile (24), shape scalars, PCA of the drawn-detail grid,
7	attribute multi-hot. Models compared on the SAME held-out splits:
8	  mean         always predicts the mean rating
9	  additive     mean by top + mean by bottom (no interaction)
10	  ridge        ridge on [t, b, t*b-free concat] features
11	  mlp          ordered-pair net: head([e_t, e_b, e_t*e_b, |e_t-e_b|]) with shared-by-slot towers, ensemble of 5
12	Splits: unseen PAIRS (5-fold), unseen TOPS (a held-out top never in training), unseen BOTTOMS.
13	Also prints the rater's own test-retest error (the ceiling) and appends a row to train_log.jsonl with --log.
14	"""
15	import argparse, json, sys, time
16	from pathlib import Path
17	
18	import numpy as np
19	import torch
20	from scipy.stats import spearmanr
21	
22	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
23	sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
24

26	def load_ratings(data):
27	    act = {}
28	    for line in open(Path(data) / "ratings.jsonl"):
29	        if not line.strip():
30	            continue
31	        r = json.loads(line)
32	        k = (r.get("rater"), r.get("sample_id"))
33	        if r.get("type") == "undo":
34	            act.pop(k, None)
35	        elif r.get("type") == "rating" and r.get("template") == "silhouette_pair" and r.get("rating"):
36	            act[k] = r
37	    by = {}
38	    for r in act.values():
39	        by.setdefault(tuple(r["pair"]), []).append(r["rating"])
40	    return by
41	
42	
43	def silhouette_features():
44	    S = json.load(open(ROOT / "src/lib/styling/silhouettes.json"))
45	    vocab = json.load(open(ROOT / "src/lib/styling/silhouette-vocab.json"))
46	    out = {}
47	    for slot in ("top", "bottom"):
48	        ss = [s for s in S if s["slot"] == slot]
49	        grid = np.array([np.array(s["detail"]["grid"]).ravel() for s in ss])
50	        g = grid - grid.mean(0)
51	        _, _, vt = np.linalg.svd(g, full_matrices=False)
52	        pca = g @ vt[:12].T
53	        pca /= pca.std() + 1e-9
54	        for i, s in enumerate(ss):
55	            a = s["attributes"]
56	            hot = []
57	            for key, spec in vocab.get(slot, {}).items():
58	                v = a.get(key)
59	                vs = v if isinstance(v, list) else ([v] if v else [])
60	                hot += [1.0 if x in vs else 0.0 for x in spec["values"]]
61	            scal = [s["aspect"], s["w_top"], s["w_mid"], s["w_low"], s["taper"] / 10, s["fill"], s["solidity"]]
62	            out[s["id"]] = (slot, np.concatenate([s["profile"], scal, pca[i], hot, [a.get("n_buttons", 0) / 10, a.get("n_pockets", 0) / 4]]))
63	    return out

70	class Net(torch.nn.Module):
71	    def __init__(self, dt, db, h=32, e=12, p=0.2):
72	        super().__init__()
73	        mk = lambda d: torch.nn.Sequential(torch.nn.Dropout(0.1), torch.nn.Linear(d, h), torch.nn.Tanh(), torch.nn.Linear(h, e), torch.nn.Tanh())
74	        self.t, self.b = mk(dt), mk(db)
75	        self.head = torch.nn.Sequential(torch.nn.Linear(4 * e, h), torch.nn.Tanh(), torch.nn.Dropout(p), torch.nn.Linear(h, 1))

78	        a, b = self.t(T), self.b(B)
79	        return self.head(torch.cat([a, b, a * b, (a - b).abs()], 1))[:, 0]

Good — the silhouette-pair model (MLP) has ρ 0.56 on unseen pairs (750 ratings, ceiling MAE 0.68). Now let me build both integrations:

  1. Tagger→silhouette attribute bridge — maps a garment's tagged attributes to the nearest library silhouette
  2. Silhouette-pair model in TypeScript — scores how well two garments' silhouettes go together, replacing the hand-rule proportionScore
Bash: Export silhouette-pair model to JSON and compute silhouette features
python3 -I -c "
import json, numpy as np
# Export the silhouette-pair MLP ensemble for TypeScript
# First retrain to get the actual model weights
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, 'experiments/silhouette-pairs')
from train import silhouette_features, load_ratings, fit_mlp, ens_predict
F = silhouette_features()
by = load_ratings('datasets/silhouettepairs')
pairs = list(by)
y = np.array([np.mean(by[p]) for p in pairs])

# Get feature dims per slot
dt = next(v[1].shape[0] for v in F.values() if v[0] == 'top')
db = next(v[1].shape[0] for v in F.values() if v[0] == 'bottom')
print(f'top features: {dt}, bottom features: {db}')

# Train the final ensemble on all data
T = np.array([F[t][1] for t, _ in pairs])
B = np.array([F[b][1] for _, b in pairs])
import torch
nets = [fit_mlp(T, B, (y - 3) / 2, seed=s) for s in range(5)]

# Compute normalisation stats
mu_t, sd_t = T.mean(0), T.std(0) + 1e-9
mu_b, sd_b = B.mean(0), B.std(0) + 1e-9

# Export
model = {
    'mu_top': mu_t.tolist(), 'sd_top': sd_t.tolist(),
    'mu_bottom': mu_b.tolist(), 'sd_bottom': sd_b.tolist(),
    'nets': []
}
for m in nets:
    w = {}
    for name, p in m.named_parameters():
        w[name] = p.detach().numpy().tolist()
    model['nets'].append(w)

with open('src/lib/styling/silhouette-pair-model.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(model, f)
import os
print(f'Model JSON size: {os.path.getsize(\"src/lib/styling/silhouette-pair-model.json\") / 1024:.1f} KB')

# also export the silhouette feature vectors for the bridge
sil_features = {}
lib = json.load(open('src/lib/styling/silhouettes.json'))
for s in lib:
    if s['id'] in F:
        sil_features[s['id']] = {'slot': F[s['id']][0], 'features': F[s['id']][1].tolist()}
with open('src/lib/styling/silhouette-features.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(sil_features, f)
print(f'Features JSON size: {os.path.getsize(\"src/lib/styling/silhouette-features.json\") / 1024:.1f} KB')

# Verify ensemble on all data
pred, _ = ens_predict(nets, T, B)
pred = pred * 2 + 3
from scipy.stats import spearmanr
print(f'Full data: MAE {np.abs(pred - y).mean():.3f}, rho {spearmanr(pred, y)[0]:.3f}')

// Maps a garment's tagger output to its closest library silhouettes, using only the attributes the tagger already tags.
// This is the lightweight bridge for stage 4a (garment → silhouette) until a CLIP-based matcher runs at upload time.
import { SILHOUETTES, silhouettesForSlot, type Silhouette, type SilhouetteAttributes, type SilhouetteMatch } from "./silhouettes";
import type { StyledItem, GarmentDetail } from "./types";

type Slot = "top" | "bottom";

const SLEEVE_MAP: Record<string, string> = {
  sleeveless: "sleeveless", strap: "strap", cap: "cap", short: "short",
  elbow: "elbow", three_quarter: "three_quarter", full: "full",
};

const FIT_ORDER = ["fitted", "regular", "loose", "oversized", "boxy"] as const;
const fitIdx = (f: string) => FIT_ORDER.indexOf(f as (typeof FIT_ORDER)[number]);

const LENGTH_MAP_TOP: Record<string, string> = {
  cropped: "cropped", short: "waist", mid: "hip", long: "thigh", full: "tunic",
};
const LENGTH_MAP_BOT: Record<string, string> = {
  cropped: "cropped", short: "shorts", mid: "capri", long: "ankle", full: "full",
};

function fitDist(a: string | undefined, b: string | undefined): number {
  if (!a || !b) return 0.3;
  const ia = fitIdx(a), ib = fitIdx(b);
  if (ia < 0 || ib < 0) return a === b ? 0 : 0.5;
  return Math.abs(ia - ib) / 4;
}

function catDist(a: string | undefined, b: string | undefined, weight = 1): number {
  if (!a || !b) return 0.2 * weight;
  return a === b ? 0 : weight;
}

function listDist(a: string[] | undefined, b: string[] | undefined): number {
  if (!a?.length || !b?.length) return 0.15;
  const sa = new Set(a), sb = new Set(b);
  let shared = 0;
  sa.forEach((x) => sb.has(x) && shared++);
  return shared > 0 ? 0 : 0.5;
}

function topDistance(d: GarmentDetail, neckline: string | null, a: SilhouetteAttributes): number {
  let dist = 0;
  dist += 2.0 * fitDist(d.fit ?? d.top_shape, a.fit);
  dist += 1.5 * catDist(d.sleeve ? SLEEVE_MAP[d.sleeve] : undefined, a.sleeve_length);
  dist += 1.0 * catDist(neckline ?? d.collar ?? undefined, a.neckline);
  dist += 0.5 * catDist(d.collar, a.collar);
  const tLen = d.silhouette === "bodycon" || d.silhouette === "fit_and_flare"
    ? undefined
    : LENGTH_MAP_TOP[(d as Record<string, string>).length ?? ""];
  dist += 1.0 * catDist(tLen, a.length);
  dist += 0.3 * listDist(d.sleeve_style ? [d.sleeve_style] : undefined, a.sleeve_style);
  dist += 0.3 * listDist(d.hem ? [d.hem] : undefined, a.hem);
  return dist;
}

function bottomDistance(d: GarmentDetail, a: SilhouetteAttributes): number {
  let dist = 0;
  dist += 2.0 * fitDist(d.fit, a.fit);
  dist += 1.5 * catDist(d.leg_shape, a.leg_shape);
  dist += 1.0 * catDist(d.waist, a.rise);
  dist += 0.5 * catDist(d.waistband, a.waistband?.[0]);
  dist += 0.5 * catDist(d.leg_end, a.length);
  dist += 0.3 * listDist(d.hem ? [d.hem] : undefined, a.hem);
  return dist;
}

/** Max possible distance per slot, used to normalise the score to 0..1. */
const MAX_DIST = { top: 6.6, bottom: 5.8 };

/**
 * Find the library silhouettes closest to a garment's tagged attributes. Returns up to 2 matches
 * with confidence scores (higher = better). Returns empty when the garment has no garment_detail
 * or its slot is not top/bottom.
 */
export function bridgeSilhouette(item: StyledItem): SilhouetteMatch {
  const d = item.garment_detail;
  if (!d) return [];
  const slot: Slot | null = item.slot === "top" || item.slot === "outerwear" ? "top" : item.slot === "bottom" ? "bottom" : null;
  if (!slot) return [];

  const candidates = silhouettesForSlot(slot);
  const scored = candidates.map((s) => {
    const raw = slot === "top"
      ? topDistance(d, item.neckline, s.attributes)
      : bottomDistance(d, s.attributes);
    return { id: s.id, score: Math.max(0, 1 - raw / MAX_DIST[slot]) };
  });
  scored.sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score);

  const best = scored[0];
  if (!best || best.score < 0.3) return [];
  const result: SilhouetteMatch = [{ id: best.id, score: round3(best.score) }];
  const sec

// The trained silhouette-pair model (experiments/silhouette-pairs/train.py) evaluated in TypeScript.
// Per-slot tower nets embed top and bottom silhouettes, then a head scores the pair.
// Weights from silhouette-pair-model.json, feature vectors from silhouette-features.json.
// Pure. Asymmetric: the top and bottom towers differ.
import model from "./silhouette-pair-model.json";
import features from "./silhouette-features.json";

type Weights = {
  "t.0.weight": number[][];
  "t.0.bias": number[];
  "t.2.weight": number[][];
  "t.2.bias": number[];
  "b.0.weight": number[][];
  "b.0.bias": number[];
  "b.2.weight": number[][];
  "b.2.bias": number[];
  "head.0.weight": number[][];
  "head.0.bias": number[];
  "head.2.weight": number[][];
  "head.2.bias": number[];
};

const NETS = (model as { nets: Weights[] }).nets;
const FEATURES = features as Record<string, { slot: string; features: number[] }>;

const affine = (x: number[], W: number[][], b: number[]): number[] =>
  b.map((bj, j) => x.reduce((s, xi, i) => s + xi * W[i][j], bj));

const tanh = (x: number[]) => x.map(Math.tanh);

function tower(x: number[], W1: number[][], b1: number[], W2: number[][], b2: number[]): number[] {
  return tanh(affine(tanh(affine(x, W1, b1)), W2, b2));
}

function forward(net: Weights, topF: number[], botF: number[]): number {
  const et = tower(topF, net["t.0.weight"], net["t.0.bias"], net["t.2.weight"], net["t.2.bias"]);
  const eb = tower(botF, net["b.0.weight"], net["b.0.bias"], net["b.2.weight"], net["b.2.bias"]);
  const z = [
    ...et.map((v, i) => v + eb[i]),
    ...et.map((v, i) => v * eb[i]),
    ...et.map((v, i) => Math.abs(v - eb[i])),
    ...et,
  ];
  const h = tanh(affine(z, net["head.0.weight"], net["head.0.bias"]));
  return h.reduce((s, hi, i) => s + hi * net["head.2.weight"][i][0], net["head.2.bias"][0]);
}

/**
 * Ensemble mean rating (1–5 scale) of how well a top silhouette goes with a bottom silhouette,
 * and the ensemble's disagreement (std in rating points). Returns null when either ID is unknown.
 */
export function silhouettePairRating(
  topId: string,
  bottomId: string,
): { rating: number; std: number } | null {
  const tf = FEATURES[topId];
  const bf = FEATURES[bottomId];
  if (!tf || !bf || tf.slot !== "top" || bf.slot !== "bottom") return null;

  const ys = NETS.map((n) => forward(n, tf.features, bf.features));
  const mean = ys.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / ys.length;
  const std = Math.sqrt(ys.reduce((a, y) => a + (y - mean) ** 2, 0) / ys.length);
  return { rating: Math.min(5, Math.max(1, 3 + 2 * mean)), std: 2 * std };
}

/** Identifies the loaded weights so retraining re-scores stored pairs. */
export const SILHOUETTE_PAIR_MODEL_ID = [
  ["top_camisole_top", "pants_straight_pants"],
  ["tee_slim_fit_t_shirt", "pants_wide_leg_pants"],
  ["shirt_classic_shirt", "skirt_a_line_skirt"],
]
  .map(([a, b]) => silhouettePairRating(a, b)?.rating.toFixed(4) ?? "?")
  .join(",");

/**
 * Silhouette compatibility for two garments mapped to 0..1 (rating 1 → 0, 5 → 1).
 * Uses the best top silhouette of one item with the best bottom silhouette of the other,
 * weighted by their match confidences.
 */
export function silhouetteModelScore(
  aMatches: { id: string; score: number }[],
  bMatches: { id: string; score: number }[],
): number | null {
  if (!aMatches.length || !bMatches.length) return null;
  const topMs = aMatches.concat(bMatches).filter((m) => FEATURES[m.id]?.slot === "top");
  const botMs = aMatches.concat(bMatches).filter((m) => FEATURES[m.id]?.slot === "bottom");
  if (!topMs.length || !botMs.length) return null;

  let total = 0;
  let weight = 0;
  for (const t of topMs) {
    for (const b of botMs) {
      const r = silhouettePairRating(t.id, b.id);
      if (r) {
        const w = t.score * b.score;
        total += w * r.rating;
        weight += w;
      }
    }
  }
  if (weight === 0) return null;
  return (total / weight - 1) / 4;
}

function topDistance(d: GarmentDetail, neckline: string | null, a: SilhouetteAttributes): number {
  let dist = 0;
  dist += 2.0 * fitDist(d.fit ?? d.top_shape, a.fit);
  dist += 1.5 * catDist(d.sleeve ? SLEEVE_MAP[d.sleeve] : undefined, a.sleeve_length);
  dist += 1.0 * catDist(neckline ?? d.collar ?? undefined, a.neckline);
  dist += 0.5 * catDist(d.collar, a.collar);
  const tLen = d.silhouette === "bodycon" || d.silhouette === "fit_and_flare"
    ? undefined
    : LENGTH_MAP_TOP[(d as Record<string, string>).length ?? ""];
  dist += 1.0 * catDist(tLen, a.length);
  dist += 0.3 * listDist(d.sleeve_style ? [d.sleeve_style] : undefined, a.sleeve_style);
  dist += 0.3 * listDist(d.hem ? [d.hem] : undefined, a.hem);
  return dist;
}

function bottomDistance(d: GarmentDetail, a: SilhouetteAttributes): number {
  let dist = 0;
  dist += 2.0 * fitDist(d.fit, a.fit);
  dist += 1.5 * catDist(d.leg_shape, a.leg_shape);
  dist += 1.0 * catDist(d.waist, a.rise);
  dist += 0.5 * catDist(d.waistband, a.waistband?.[0]);
  dist += 0.5 * catDist(d.leg_end, a.length);
  dist += 0.3 * listDist(d.hem ? [d.hem] : undefined, a.hem);
  return dist;
}
+++ new
function topDistance(d: GarmentDetail, item: StyledItem, a: SilhouetteAttributes): number {
  let dist = 0;
  const fitVal = item.fit ?? (d.top_shape === "fitted" ? "fitted" : d.top_shape === "boxy" ? "oversized" : undefined);
  dist += 2.0 * fitDist(fitVal, a.fit);
  dist += 1.5 * catDist(d.sleeve ? SLEEVE_MAP[d.sleeve] : undefined, a.sleeve_length);
  dist += 1.0 * catDist(item.neckline ?? d.collar ?? undefined, a.neckline);
  dist += 0.5 * catDist(d.collar, a.collar);
  const tLen = d.silhouette === "bodycon" || d.silhouette === "fit_and_flare"
    ? undefined
    : LENGTH_MAP_TOP[item.length ?? ""];
  dist += 1.0 * catDist(tLen, a.length);
  dist += 0.3 * listDist(d.sleeve_style ? [d.sleeve_style] : undefined, a.sleeve_style);
  dist += 0.3 * listDist(d.hem ? [d.hem] : undefined, a.hem);
  return dist;
}

function bottomDistance(d: GarmentDetail, item: StyledItem, a: SilhouetteAttributes): number {
  let dist = 0;
  dist += 2.0 * fitDist(item.fit ?? undefined, a.fit);
  dist += 1.5 * catDist(d.leg_shape, a.leg_shape);
  dist += 1.0 * catDist(d.waist, a.rise);
  dist += 0.5 * catDist(d.waistband, a.waistband?.[0]);
  dist += 0.5 * catDist(d.leg_end, a.length);
  dist += 0.3 * listDist(d.hem ? [d.hem] : undefined, a.hem);
  return dist;
}

function forward(net: Weights, topF: number[], botF: number[]): number {
  const et = tower(topF, net["t.0.weight"], net["t.0.bias"], net["t.2.weight"], net["t.2.bias"]);
  const eb = tower(botF, net["b.0.weight"], net["b.0.bias"], net["b.2.weight"], net["b.2.bias"]);
  const z = [
    ...et.map((v, i) => v + eb[i]),
    ...et.map((v, i) => v * eb[i]),

}

function forward(net: Weights, topF: number[], botF: number[]): number {
  const et = tower(topF, net["t.1.weight"], net["t.1.bias"], net["t.3.weight"], net["t.3.bias"]);
  const eb = tower(botF, net["b.1.weight"], net["b.1.bias"], net["b.3.weight"], net["b.3.bias"]);
  const z = [

    ...et.map((v, i) => v * eb[i]),

  return h.reduce((s, hi, i) => s + hi * net["head.3.weight"][i][0], net["head.3.bias"][0]);

The affine function crashes because the weight matrix W is transposed compared to what I expect. In PyTorch, Linear(in, out) stores weight as [out, in], so W[i] where i is the input index doesn't work — I need W[j][i] or transpose the indexing. Let me fix the affine operation.

Bash: Check weight shapes in exported model
python3 -c "

n = m['nets'][0]
import numpy as np

    print(f'{k}: {a.shape}')
"

t.3.bias: (12,)

head.3.weight: (1, 32)
head.3.bias: (1,)

Right — PyTorch stores [out_features, in_features], so W is [out, in]. My affine indexes W[i][j] where i is input index and j is output index, but the matrix is the other way around. Fix: use W[j][i] instead.

Edit: /home/palak_raisinghani/my/courses/Fashion_Assist/src/lib/styling/silhouettePair.ts

+++ new
const affine = (x: number[], W: number[][], b: number[]): number[] =>
  b.map((bj, j) => x.reduce((s, xi, i) => s + xi * W[j][i], bj));

Bash: Verify Python model outputs for comparison
experiments/embeddings/.venv/bin/python -I -c "
import json, numpy as np, sys, torch
sys.path.insert(0, 'experiments/silhouette-pairs')
from train import silhouette_features, fit_mlp, load_ratings

F = silhouette_features()
by = load_ratings('datasets/silhouettepairs')
pairs = list(by)
y = np.array([np.mean(by[p]) for p in pairs])
T = np.array([F[t][1] for t, _ in pairs])
B = np.array([F[b][1] for _, b in pairs])
nets = [fit_mlp(T, B, (y - 3) / 2, seed=s) for s in range(5)]

test_pairs = [
    ('top_camisole_top', 'pants_straight_pants'),
    ('tee_slim_fit_t_shirt', 'pants_wide_leg_pants'),
    ('shirt_classic_shirt', 'skirt_a_line_skirt'),
    ('top_blouse_top', 'pants_skinny_jeans'),
    ('tee_oversized_t_shirt', 'shorts_bermuda_shorts'),
]

for t, b in test_pairs:
    ft = torch.tensor(F[t][1], dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(0)
    fb = torch.tensor(F[b][1], dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(0)
    ys = []
    for m in nets:
        m.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            a_e, b_e = m.t(ft), m.b(fb)
            z = torch.cat([a_e, b_e, a_e * b_e, (a_e - b_e).abs()], 1)
            ys.append(m.head(z).item())
    mean = np.mean(ys)
    std = np.std(ys)
    print(f'{t:30s} {b:30s} {3 + 2*mean:.3f} ±{2*std:.3f}')
" 2>&1

python3 -c "
import json, numpy as np

model = json.load(open('src/lib/styling/silhouette-pair-model.json'))
feats = json.load(open('src/lib/styling/silhouette-features.json'))

def affine(x, W, b):
    W = np.array(W); b = np.array(b)
    return x @ W.T + b  # W is [out, in] (PyTorch convention)

def tower(x, W1, b1, W2, b2):
    return np.tanh(affine(np.tanh(affine(x, W1, b1)), W2, b2))

def forward(net, tf, bf):
    et = tower(tf, net['t.1.weight'], net['t.1.bias'], net['t.3.weight'], net['t.3.bias'])
    eb = tower(bf, net['b.1.weight'], net['b.1.bias'], net['b.3.weight'], net['b.3.bias'])
    z = np.concatenate([et, eb, et*eb, np.abs(et-eb)])
    h = np.tanh(affine(z, net['head.0.weight'], net['head.0.bias']))
    return float(h @ np.array(net['head.3.weight']).T + net['head.3.bias'][0])

def rating(top_id, bot_id):
    tf = np.array(feats[top_id]['features'])
    bf = np.array(feats[bot_id]['features'])
    ys = [forward(n, tf, bf) for n in model['nets']]
    mean = np.mean(ys)
    std = np.std(ys)
    return 3 + 2*mean, 2*std

pairs = [
    ('top_camisole_top', 'pants_straight_pants'),
    ('tee_slim_fit_t_shirt', 'pants_wide_leg_pants'),
    ('shirt_classic_shirt', 'skirt_a_line_skirt'),
    ('top_blouse_top', 'pants_skinny_jeans'),
    ('tee_oversized_t_shirt', 'shorts_bermuda_shorts'),
]
for t, b in pairs:
    r, s = rating(t, b)
    print(f'{t:30s} {b:30s} {r:.3f} +-{s:.3f}')
"

python3 -c "
import json, random, numpy as np

model = json.load(open('src/lib/styling/silhouette-pair-model.json'))
feats = json.load(open('src/lib/styling/silhouette-features.json'))
tops = [k for k, v in feats.items() if v['slot'] == 'top']
bots = [k for k, v in feats.items() if v['slot'] == 'bottom']

def affine(x, W, b):
    W = np.array(W); b = np.array(b)
    return x @ W.T + b

def tower(x, W1, b1, W2, b2):
    return np.tanh(affine(np.tanh(affine(x, W1, b1)), W2, b2))

def forward(net, tf, bf):
    et = tower(tf, net['t.1.weight'], net['t.1.bias'], net['t.3.weight'], net['t.3.bias'])
    eb = tower(bf, net['b.1.weight'], net['b.1.bias'], net['b.3.weight'], net['b.3.bias'])
    z = np.concatenate([et, eb, et*eb, np.abs(et-eb)])
    h = np.tanh(affine(z, net['head.0.weight'], net['head.0.bias']))
    out = h @ np.array(net['head.3.weight']).T + net['head.3.bias']
    return float(out[0])

def rating(top_id, bot_id):
    tf = np.array(feats[top_id]['features'])
    bf = np.array(feats[bot_id]['features'])
    ys = [forward(n, tf, bf) for n in model['nets']]
    mean = float(np.mean(ys))
    std = float(np.std(ys))
    return min(5, max(1, 3 + 2*mean)), 2*std

random.seed(42)
pairs = set()
# a fixed spread plus random sampling for coverage
fixed = [
    ('top_camisole_top', 'pants_straight_pants'),
    ('tee_slim_fit_t_shirt', 'pants_wide_leg_pants'),
    ('shirt_classic_shirt', 'skirt_a_line_skirt'),
    ('top_blouse_top', 'pants_skinny_jeans'),
    ('tee_oversized_t_shirt', 'shorts_bermuda_shorts'),
]
for p in fixed:
    pairs.add(p)
while len(pairs) < 20:
    pairs.add((random.choice(tops), random.choice(bots)))

golden = []
for t, b in sorted(pairs):
    r, s = rating(t, b)
    golden.append({'top': t, 'bottom': b, 'rating': r, 'std': s})

with open('tests/fixtures/silhouette-pair-golden.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(golden, f, indent=1)
print(f'{len(golden)} golden pairs written')
"

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import golden from "./fixtures/silhouette-pair-golden.json";
import { silhouetteModelScore, silhouettePairRating } from "@/lib/styling/silhouettePair";
import { bridgeSilhouette } from "@/lib/styling/silhouetteBridge";
import type { StyledItem } from "@/lib/styling/types";

describe("silhouette-pair model in TypeScript", () => {
  it("matches the Python model on stored examples", () => {
    for (const g of golden) {
      const r = silhouettePairRating(g.top, g.bottom);
      expect(r).not.toBeNull();
      expect(r!.rating).toBeCloseTo(g.rating, 5);
      expect(r!.std).toBeCloseTo(g.std, 5);
    }
  });
  it("stays on the 1-5 scale", () => {
    for (const g of golden) {
      const r = silhouettePairRating(g.top, g.bottom)!.rating;
      expect(r).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
      expect(r).toBeLessThanOrEqual(5);
    }
  });
  it("is null for an unknown id or a slot mismatch", () => {
    expect(silhouettePairRating("not_a_real_id", "pants_straight_pants")).toBeNull();
    // top id passed as the bottom slot
    expect(silhouettePairRating("top_camisole_top", "top_camisole_top")).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe("silhouetteModelScore", () => {
  it("maps the pair rating to 0..1 using the best-matching silhouettes", () => {
    const s = silhouetteModelScore(
      [{ id: "top_camisole_top", score: 1 }],
      [{ id: "pants_straight_pants", score: 1 }],
    )!;
    const r = silhouettePairRating("top_camisole_top", "pants_straight_pants")!.rating;
    expect(s).toBeCloseTo((r - 1) / 4, 9);
  });
  it("is null when either side has no matches", () => {
    expect(silhouetteModelScore([], [{ id: "pants_straight_pants", score: 1 }])).toBeNull();
    expect(silhouetteModelScore([{ id: "top_camisole_top", score: 1 }], [])).toBeNull();
  });
  it("weights several candidates by confidence", () => {
    const s = silhouetteModelScore(
      [
        { id: "top_camisole_top", score: 0.9 },
        { id: "top_blouse_top", score: 0.1 },
      ],
      [{ id: "pants_straight_pants", score: 1 }],
    )!;
    expect(s).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
    expect(s).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1);
  });
});

describe("bridgeSilhouette", () => {

    id: "x",

## Colour-pair architecture check: hex digits and 10 layers (2026-10-24)
`experiments/colour-pairs/arch_compare.py`, 654 rated pairs, 5-fold twice, Spearman / MAE in rating points. All variants symmetric (both orders trained, both averaged).
| variant | unseen pairs | unseen colours |
|---|---|---|
| shipped (shared encoder, Lab features, 4 layers) | 0.66 / 0.68 | 0.64 / 0.71 |
| 10 layers x 32 on Lab features | 0.60 / 0.75 | 0.59 / 0.75 |
| 10 layers x 32 on the 12 hex digits | 0.25 / 0.98 | 0.05 / 1.02 |
| 10 layers x 32 on RGB | 0.08 / 0.99 | 0.14 / 0.98 |
| 2 layers on Lab / hex / RGB | 0.63 / 0.50 / 0.52 | 0.61 / 0.31 / 0.48 |
Conclusion: raw hex digits are a poor input (a digit's size says nothing about the colour: #a8 and #a9 are the same colour, #0f and #10 are far apart), and depth hurts with this much data (10 layers worse than 2 on the same Lab input, and far worse than the shipped design). The shipped design already beats the rater's own test-retest (Spearman 0.44 on 49 repeats). Smoothing the rater's drift is a data and loss question (more raters, one rater offset and scale per person, more rated pairs), not a depth question.

## Rater-aware colour training; model retrained on 685 pairs (2026-10-24)
- **Why:** a second rater is joining, and the owner's own repeats agree only 76% within 1 point (MAE 0.86), so consistency is the colour model's weak spot. Pooling raters naively would mix scales.
- **How** (`experiments/colour-pairs/raters.py`): each rater r is `rating = a_r + b_r * y(pair) + noise_r`. y is the shared network on the reference rater's scale (the rater with most ratings, a = 0, b = 1). Training alternates: fit the network on every rater's ratings mapped to the reference scale, weighted by 1 / (repeat noise + 0.05); then refit a_r, b_r, shrunk toward (0, 1) with a prior of 20 ratings. With one rater it is the plain training. The rater scales and weights are stored in `model.json` (the closet ignores them). Cross-validation folds by pair, so all raters' ratings of one pair stay together, and each rater is checked on their own scale.
- **Test:** a simulated harsh, narrow, noisier second rater: the scale is recovered (offset -0.5, stretch 0.6) and pooling does not hurt.
- **Retrained** on 685 pairs (734 ratings, 1 rater): unseen pairs 0.65, unseen colours 0.61. Shipped to `src/lib/styling/colour-pair-model.json`; golden fixture regenerated.
- **Fingerprint:** `COLOUR_MODEL_ID` (the model's ratings on 4 fixed pairs) is now in the item fingerprint, so a retrained model re-scores stored pairs; before, only a config change did.
- **Retrained (same day) on 1020 pairs** (1109 ratings, all samples rated): owner's repeats now 85% within 1 point (MAE 0.62, was 76% / 0.86); unseen pairs 0.69, unseen colours 0.64 (were 0.65 / 0.61). Shipped; golden fixture regenerated.

## Garment -> silhouette pool: product-only shop photos joined to the old pool (2026-10-24)
- **Why:** a third of the first pool's cut-outs (photos of models, cut by the u2net clothing segmenter) were torn, and the pool was Princess Polly only, so it was skewed toward camis, halters, wide-leg pants and minis.
- **How** (`experiments/silhouette-match/web_pool.py`): public Shopify feeds (`/products.json`; robots.txt checked, 1 feed request/s, honest user agent). Per top or bottom, CLIP (ViT-B-32) picks the product's photo most likely to be the garment alone (flat-lay / ghost mannequin, p >= 0.6). The background is a smooth surface fitted to the photo border and flood-filled away, so no segmentation model and no tearing. The same completeness check as the pool, "accept" only; near-copies of an outline already kept from the shop (same cut, other colour) are skipped. Dresses, outerwear, knitwear (incl. turtlenecks / mock necks), sets, swim and underwear are skipped (no library drawings). Each style bucket (`KINDS`, e.g. jeans, cami, corset) is capped at 45 in the joined pool, so the denim shops could not keep adding jeans.
- **Joined pool** (`skew.py`): the

## Garment -> silhouette matcher (4a): trained on 671 real labels (2026-10-25)
- **Why:** the matcher was trained on synthetic cloth renders only (`experiments/silhouette-match/synth.py`); real garments need real labels to close the sim-to-real gap.
- **Trained** (`train.py --labels --epochs 80`) on the 671 clean labels (of 843; bad cut-outs and "none fit" excluded), 5-fold cross-validated so each garment is scored by a model that never saw it:
| method | top-1 | top-3 | top-5 | MRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| outline distance only | 16.8% | 34.6% | 43.8% | 0.31 |
| CLIP zero-shot | 36.4% | 65.0% | 78.8% | 0.54 |
| trained on synthetic only | 30.3% | 52.0% | 62.4% | 0.46 |
| **trained + real labels** | **80.9%** | **92.5%** | **95.5%** | **0.87** |
- Well above the 60% top-5 target. Saved to `datasets/silhouette-match/head_v1.npz`. Not yet run at upload time (no CLIP call in the app's tagging path); `silhouetteBridge.ts` is the stand-in until it is.

## Silhouette-pair model (4b) ported to TypeScript; silhouette bridge added; both plugged into pairScore (2026-10-25)
- **Silhouette bridge** (`src/lib/styling/silhouetteBridge.ts`): maps the tagger's already-tagged fields (fit, sleeve, neckline/collar, leg_shape, waist/rise, hem, ...) to the closest library silhouette(s) by a hand-written weighted distance, since the garment -> silhouette matcher (4a) does not run at upload time yet. Returns up to 2 matches with a confidence each; empty when the garment has no `garment_detail` or is not a top/bottom/outerwear.
- **Silhouette-pair model** (`src/lib/styling/silhouettePair.ts`): the trained MLP (`experiments/silhouette-pairs/train.py`, 750 rated pairs, unseen-pairs Spearman 0.56 vs the rater's own ceiling MAE 0.68) evaluated in TypeScript from weights in `silhouette-pair-model.json` (1.5 MB) and silhouette feature vectors in `silhouette-features.json` (262 KB; 171-dim top / 192-dim bottom: outline profile + shape scalars + PCA of the detail grid + attribute multi-hot). Pattern copied from `colourPair.ts`: an ensemble of 5 nets, golden-tested against the exact exported weights (`tests/silhouette-pair.test.ts`, `tests/fixtures/silhouette-pair-golden.json`).

Here's the pipeline, in fixed order, with what's now hooked in:

# Stage Model/method live in the app State
1 Segmentation detect.v1 Live, unchanged
2 Tagging tagger.v11 Live, unchanged
3a Colour picker rule-based (hex + area share) Live, unchanged
3b Colour-pair model trained MLP ensemble (colourPair.ts) Live, weight 1 (model only)
4a Garment → silhouette matcher trained (head_v1.npz, CLIP + outline), not called at upload time Trained but not wired in — see below
4b Silhouette-pair model trained MLP ensemble (silhouettePair.ts), fed by silhouetteBridge.ts Newly live this session, weight 1 (model only)
5 pairScore combines 3b + 4b + hand rules (formality, style, season) Live, now using the real silhouette model for proportion instead of the old fit/length-only rule
6 Vision ranker rank.v3, blend 0.7/0.3 on uncertain pairs Live, unchanged
7 Matches top 5, min 0.5 Live, unchanged

The gap at 4a→4b: stage 4a (the trained CLIP matcher, 95.5% top-5) isn't called when a garment is tagged — there's no CLIP inference in the upload/tagging path yet. So stage 4b doesn't get real matcher output; it gets silhouetteBridge.ts, a hand-written distance over the tagger's own fields (fit, sleeve, neckline, leg_shape, etc.), picking the closest library silhouette(s) as a stand-in. That bridge output is what 4b actually blends into pairScore.

What's remaining: - Wire 4a into the live pipeline (a CLIP call at tagging time) so 4b gets real matcher picks instead of the bridge's attribute-nearest-neighbour guess. - The full-sleeve-shirt silhouette picture you meant to drop in silhouettes/new/ never arrived — folder's still empty. - Second rater's colour pairs (3b) — rater-aware retrain once they have ~300 rated pairs. - Outerwear pairs aren't covered by either trained model yet (fall back to the hand rule only). - Current session's work (4b port + bridge + pairScore wiring) is uncommitted — waiting on your go-ahead from my last message.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Match one live garment cut-out to its closest library silhouettes, using the trained head (stage 4a).

Usage: ../embeddings/.venv/bin/python -I match_one.py <cutout.png> <top|bottom> [--model head_v1.npz]
The input must have a transparent background (as @imgly/background-removal produces): it is composited onto
white and the garment mask is read from alpha >= 128, matching how the training images were prepared.
Prints JSON to stdout: the top 2 silhouette ids with a softmax confidence within the garment's slot, best
first, e.g. [{"id": "tee_slim_fit_t_shirt", "score": 0.81}, {"id": "top_blouse_top", "score": 0.14}].
Prints "[]" (not an error) when the cut-out has no visible garment or the slot has no silhouettes.
Called from the app via src/lib/ai/silhouetteMatch.ts, one subprocess per item (a few seconds: CLIP loads fresh
each time). Any failure here should be caught by the caller, which falls back to the attribute-based bridge.
"""
import argparse, json, sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))  # -I leaves the script folder off the path; features.py and train.py are ours
from features import Extractor  # noqa: E402
from train import IDS, SLOT, load_head  # noqa: E402

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("cutout")
ap.add_argument("slot", choices=["top", "bottom"])
ap.add_argument("--model", default=str(ROOT / "datasets/silhouette-match/head_v1.npz"))
args = ap.parse_args()


def load_cutout(path):
    im = Image.open(path).convert("RGBA")
    alpha = np.array(im)[:, :, 3]
    mask = alpha >= 128
    white = Image.new("RGB", im.size, (255, 255, 255))
    white.paste(im, (0, 0), im)  # alpha as the paste mask: only the garment lands on the white canvas
    return white, mask


def main():
    img, mask = load_cutout(args.cutout)
    idx = np.nonzero(SLOT == args.slot)[0]
    if not mask.any() or len(idx) == 0:
        print(json.dumps([]))
        return
    f = Extractor().features([img], [mask])[0]
    logits = load_head(args.model).logits(f)[idx]
    order = np.argsort(-logits)[:2]
    e = np.exp(logits - logits.max())
    p = e / e.sum()
    print(json.dumps([{"id": IDS[idx[i]], "score": round(float(p[i]), 4)} for i in order]))


main()

Write: /home/palak_raisinghani/my/courses/Fashion_Assist/src/lib/ai/silhouetteMatch.ts
// Stage 4a, live: matches a garment cut-out to its closest library silhouettes by shelling out to the trained
// CLIP + outline model (experiments/silhouette-match/match_one.py, head_v1.npz). There is no CLIP implementation
// in this app, so inference runs out of process; this is the only place src/ calls into a Python script at
// request time. A few seconds per call (the model loads fresh each run) — always called from a background
// task (see the tag route's `after()`), never inline in a request a user is waiting on.
import { execFile } from "node:child_process";
import { mkdtemp, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { promisify } from "node:util";
import { SilhouetteMatchSchema, type SilhouetteMatch } from "@/lib/styling/silhouettes";

const run = promisify(execFile);
const ROOT = process.cwd();
const PYTHON = path.join(ROOT, "experiments/embeddings/.venv/bin/python");
const SCRIPT = path.join(ROOT, "experiments/silhouette-match/match_one.py");

/**
 * Matches one garment cut-out (a transparent-background PNG, as the upload pipeline's background removal
 * produces) to its closest library silhouettes. `slot` must be "top" or "bottom" (outerwear is matched
 * against the top library, same convention as silhouetteBridge.ts). Returns [] — never throws — on any
 * failure (missing venv, bad image, timeout, malformed output), so callers can always fall back to the
 * attribute-based bridge without special-casing errors.
 */
export async function matchSilhouette(
  cutoutPng: Buffer,
  slot: "top" | "bottom",
): Promise<SilhouetteMatch> {
  let dir: string | null = null;
  try {
    dir = await mkdtemp(path.join(tmpdir(), "sil-match-"));
    const file = path.join(dir, "cutout.png");
    await writeFile(file, cutoutPng);
    const { stdout } = await run(PYTHON, ["-I", SCRIPT, file, slot], { timeout: 30_000 });
    const parsed = SilhouetteMatchSchema.safeParse(JSON.parse(stdout));
    return parsed.success ? parsed.data : [];
  } catch (e) {
    console.error("silhouette match failed:", e instanceof Error ? e.message : "unknown");
    return [];
  } finally {
    if (dir) await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }).catch(() => undefined);
  }
}

          await auth.supabase.from("items").update({ silhouette_matches: matches }).eq("id", id);
        }
      } catch (e) {
        console.error("silhouette match step failed:", e instanceof Error ? e.message : "unknown");
      }
    }
    await refreshPairsForItem(userId, id).catch(() => undefined);
  });
  return ok({ rejected: false });
}

import { describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";

const execFileMock = vi.fn();
vi.mock("node:child_process", () => ({ execFile: (...args: unknown[]) => execFileMock(...args) }));

// execFile promisified calls back (err, {stdout, stderr}); drive it the same way node:util.promisify would.
function mockResult(stdout: string) {
  execFileMock.mockImplementation((...args: unknown[]) => {
    const cb = args[args.length - 1] as (err: Error | null, r?: { stdout: string; stderr: string }) => void;
    cb(null, { stdout, stderr: "" });
  });
}
function mockFailure(err: Error) {
  execFileMock.mockImplementation((...args: unknown[]) => {
    const cb = args[args.length - 1] as (err: Error | null) => void;
    cb(err);
  });
}

describe("matchSilhouette", () => {
  it("parses a valid match array from the subprocess", async () => {
    mockResult(JSON.stringify([{ id: "tee_slim_fit_t_shirt", score: 0.81 }]));
    const { matchSilhouette } = await import("@/lib/ai/silhouetteMatch");
    const r = await matchSilhouette(Buffer.from("fake-png"), "top");
    expect(r).toEqual([{ id: "tee_slim_fit_t_shirt", score: 0.81 }]);
  });
  it("returns [] when the subprocess fails", async () => {
    mockFailure(new Error("spawn ENOENT"));
    const { matchSilhouette } = await import("@/lib/ai/silhouetteMatch");
    const r = await matchSilhouette(Buffer.from("fake-png"), "top");
    expect(r).toEqual([]);
  });
  it("returns [] when the subprocess prints something that isn't a valid match array", async () => {
    mockResult("not json");
    const { matchSilhouette: m1 } = await import("@/lib/ai/silhouetteMatch");
    expect(await m1(Buffer.from("x"), "top")).toEqual([]);
    mockResult(JSON.stringify([{ id: "not_a_real_silhouette_id", score: 0.5 }]));
    const { matchSilhouette: m2 } = await import("@/lib/ai/silhouetteMatch");
    expect(await m2(Buffer.from("x"), "top")).toEqual([]);
  });
  it("passes an empty result through unchanged", async () => {
    mockResult("[]");
    const { matchSilhouette } = await import("@/lib/ai/silhouetteMatch");
    expect(await matchSilhouette(Buffer.from("x"), "bottom")).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe("pairScore falls back to the attribute bridge", () => {
  const top: StyledItem = {
    id: "top1",
    slot: "top",
    category: "tshirt",
    colors: [],
    pattern: "solid",
    formality: 3,
    warmth: null,
    seasons: null,
    style_tags: null,
    occasions: ["casual"],
    neckline: "round",
    statement_level: 1,
    metal_tone: null,
    fit: "fitted",
    garment_detail: { sleeve: "sleeveless", collar: "none" },
  };
  const bottom: StyledItem = {
    id: "bot1",
    slot: "bottom",
    category: "jeans",
    colors: [],
    pattern: "solid",
    formality: 3,
    warmth: null,
    seasons: null,
    style_tags: null,
    occasions: ["casual"],
    neckline: null,
    statement_level: 1,
    metal_tone: null,
    fit: "fitted",
    garment_detail: { leg_shape: "straight", waist: "natural" },
  };
  it("an item with stored matches uses them, not the bridge", () => {
    const withReal = pairScore(
      { ...top, silhouette_matches: [{ id: "tee_slim_fit_t_shirt", score: 1 }] },
      bottom,
    );
    const withBridge = pairScore(top, bottom); // no stored matches: falls back to bridgeSilhouette(top)
    // both produce a number; they need not be equal, but both must be defined and on the 0..1 scale
    expect(withReal.parts.proportion).not.toBeNull();
    expect(withBridge.parts.proportion).not.toBeNull();
  });
  it("an explicitly empty match array falls back to the bridge too, not straight to the hand rule", () => {
    const empty = pairScore({ ...top, silhouette_matches: [] }, bottom);
    const missing = pairScore({ ...top, silhouette_matches: undefined }, bottom);
    expect(empty.parts.proportion).toBeCloseTo(missing.parts.proportion!, 9);
  });
});

what do I have to do ?
Claude's response

The simplest path — no CLI, no login flow:

  1. Go to your Supabase project dashboard → SQL Editor (left sidebar).
  2. Paste this and click Run:
alter table items add column if not exists silhouette_matches jsonb;

That's it — one statement, additive only (just adds a nullable column, doesn't touch any existing data). Once it's run, the feature is live: the next time any item gets tagged, the tag route will call the trained matcher and store its result there.

If you'd rather I do it myself, the other option is you run npx supabase login in a terminal here (it opens a browser to authenticate), then tell me and I'll run npm run db:push to apply it properly through the CLI. But the dashboard paste is faster if you just want it done now.

// One-off backfill: runs the live garment -> silhouette matcher (stage 4a, experiments/silhouette-match/match_one.py)
// against every already-tagged item that predates this feature, so existing closets benefit immediately, not just
// items tagged from now on. Usage: node --env-file=.env.local scripts/backfill-silhouette-matches.mjs [--user-email you@x.com]
// Defaults to the demo user (DEMO_EMAIL). Safe to re-run: only touches items where silhouette_matches is still null.
import { execFile } from "node:child_process";
import { mkdtemp, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { promisify } from "node:util";
import { createClient } from "@supabase/supabase-js";

const run = promisify(execFile);
const ROOT = process.cwd();
const PYTHON = path.join(ROOT, "experiments/embeddings/.venv/bin/python");
const SCRIPT = path.join(ROOT, "experiments/silhouette-match/match_one.py");

const { NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: url, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY: key, DEMO_EMAIL } = process.env;
const emailArgIdx = process.argv.indexOf("--user-email");
const email = emailArgIdx >= 0 ? process.argv[emailArgIdx + 1] : DEMO_EMAIL;
if (!url || !key || !email) {
  console.error("Set NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and DEMO_EMAIL, or pass --user-email.");
  process.exit(1);
}

const admin = createClient(url, key, { auth: { persistSession: false, autoRefreshToken: false } });
const matchSlotOf = (slot) => (slot === "top" || slot === "outerwear" ? "top" : slot === "bottom" ? "bottom" : null);

async function matchSilhouette(cutoutPng, slot) {
  const dir = await mkdtemp(path.join(tmpdir(), "sil-match-"));
  try {
    const file = path.join(dir, "cutout.png");
    await writeFile(file, cutoutPng);
    const { stdout } = await run(PYTHON, ["-I", SCRIPT, file, slot], { timeout: 30_000 });
    return JSON.parse(stdout);
  } finally {
    await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

// Throwaway: builds a local HTML page comparing each backfilled demo item's real photo against its matched
// silhouette's reference drawing, so the match quality can be eyeballed directly. Not part of the app.
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";
import { createClient } from "@supabase/supabase-js";

const { NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: url, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY: key, DEMO_EMAIL } = process.env;
const admin = createClient(url, key, { auth: { persistSession: false, autoRefreshToken: false } });
const { data: list } = await admin.auth.admin.listUsers({ perPage: 1000 });
const user = list?.users.find((u) => u.email === DEMO_EMAIL);

const { data: items } = await admin
  .from("items")
  .select("id, slot, category, subcategory, cutout_path, silhouette_matches")
  .eq("user_id", user.id)
  .not("silhouette_matches", "is", null)
  .order("created_at", { ascending: false })
  .limit(5);

const toDataUrl = async (buf, mime) => `data:${mime};base64,${buf.toString("base64")}`;

const rows = [];
for (const item of items) {
  const { data: blob } = await admin.storage.from("wardrobe").download(item.cutout_path);
  const itemUrl = await toDataUrl(Buffer.from(await blob.arrayBuffer()), "image/png");
  const matches = await Promise.all(
    (item.silhouette_matches ?? []).map(async (m) => {
      const libPath = path.join(process.cwd(), "datasets/silhouettes/library", `${m.id}_clean.png`);
      const buf = await readFile(libPath).catch(() => null);
      return { id: m.id, score: m.score, url: buf ? await toDataUrl(buf, "image/png") : null };
    }),
  );
  rows.push({ label: item.subcategory ?? item.category, itemUrl, matches });
}

const html = `<!doctype html><html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Silhouette match review</title>
<style>
body{font-family:system-ui;background:#111;color:#eee;padding:24px}
.row{display:flex;gap:24px;align-items:flex-start;border-bottom:1px solid #333;padding:20px 0}
.row img{height:220px;object-fit:contain;background:#fff;border-radius:8px}
.label{width:220px;font-weight:600}
.match{text-align:center;font-size:13px}
.score{color:#9cf}
</style></head><body>
<h1>Silhouette match review (demo account)</h1>
${rows
  .map(
    (r) => `<div class="row">
  <div class="label">${r.label}</div>
  <img src="${r.itemUrl}" alt="item photo">
  <span style="font-size:24px;align-self:center">&rarr;</span>
  ${r.matches
    .map(
      (m) =>
        `<div class="match">${m.url ? `<img src="${m.url}" alt="${m.id}">` : "(no image)"}<br>${m.id}<br><span class="score">${m.score}</span></div>`,
    )
    .join("")}
</div>`,
  )
  .join("\n")}
</body></html>`;

const out = path.join(process.cwd(), ".match-review.html");
await (await import("node:fs/promises")).writeFile(out, html);
console.log(`Written to ${out}`);

Found it. In src/components/garment-splitter.tsx line 90, the photo <img> uses w-full object-contain with a max-h-[60vh] cap. That combination forces the image into a box whose aspect ratio doesn't match the photo's own aspect ratio whenever the height cap kicks in (any portrait photo taller than ~60% of viewport width) — so object-contain letterboxes it, leaving blank margins. But the detection boxes are positioned as percentages of the wrapping frame, not the actual visible image content, so boxes land in the letterbox margin instead of on the garment. Since detection runs on original image pixels regardless of aspect ratio, uploading a batch of mixed portrait/landscape photos makes each review screen misalign differently — which reads as "messy overlap" as you flip through them.

The fix is to stop forcing a mismatched box and let the image size itself naturally within the height cap, so the wrapping frame's bounds always exactly equal the visible image (no letterboxing, no coordinate drift):

Edit: /home/palak_raisinghani/my/courses/Fashion_Assist/src/components/garment-splitter.tsx
--- old
        <img src={url} alt="Photo to add" className="block max-h-[60vh] w-full object-contain" />
+++ new
        {/* no w-full/object-contain: letterboxing would shift the frame's bounds away from the visible
            image, and the boxes below are positioned as percentages of this element's own box */}
        <img src={url} alt="Photo to add" className="block max-h-[60vh] max-w-full" />

Found and fixed: src/components/garment-splitter.tsx line 90-92. The review photo's <img> had w-full object-contain combined with max-h-[60vh] — forcing it into a box whose aspect ratio often didn't match the photo's own ratio (any portrait photo, which is most phone photos). object-contain then letterboxed it, leaving blank margins. But the detection boxes are positioned as percentages of the wrapping frame, not the actual visible image — so boxes landed in the blank margin, misaligned by a different amount for every photo depending on its aspect ratio. Flipping through a batch of mixed-orientation uploads, each misaligned differently, is exactly the "messy overlap" you saw.

Fixed by dropping w-full/object-contain so the image sizes itself naturally (max-w-full, height auto, capped at max-h-[60vh]) — the frame always exactly matches the visible image now, so box percentages line up regardless of orientation, and the queue (one GarmentSplitter dialog at a time, confirmed correct in uploader.tsx) was never actually the problem.

Try uploading a batch again — the dev server should hot-reload this. Let me know if the boxes land correctly now.

+++ new
        {items.map((it, i) => (
          // the box is an outline only (no fill, no pointer events): overlapping boxes stay legible as crossing
          // lines instead of stacking into a muddy transparent blob, and never steal a tap meant for another
          // garment's badge. The badge is a fixed-size target anchored at the corner, so it is always easy to
          // hit regardless of how small or how overlapped the detected box is.
          <div key={i} className="pointer-events-none absolute" style={pct(it.box)}>
            <div
              className={`absolute inset-0 border-2 ${it.on ? "border-[var(--light)]" : "border-dashed border-white/35"}`}
            />
            <button
              type="button"
              onPointerDown={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
              onClick={() => toggle(i)}
              aria-pressed={it.on}
              aria-label={`${it.on ? "Leave out" : "Include"} ${it.label}`}
              className={`pointer-events-auto absolute -top-2 -left-2 flex h-8 min-w-8 items-center justify-center gap-1 rounded-full px-2 text-xs font-semibold shadow-md transition-transform active:scale-95 ${
                it.on
                  ? "bg-[var(--light)] text-black"
                  : "border border-white/40 bg-black/85 text-white/70"
              }`}
            >
              {it.on ? <Check size={14} aria-hidden="true" /> : <X size={14} aria-hidden="true" />}
              {i + 1}
            </button>
          </div>
        ))}

24	export async function listItems(
25	  supabase: SupabaseClient,
26	  filters: { slot?: string; season?: string; q?: string } = {},
27	): Promise<ItemRow[]> {
28	  let query = supabase
29	    .from("items")
30	    .select(
31	      "id, slot, category, subcategory, tags_confirmed, fit, pattern_detail, garment_detail, rejection_reason, thumb_path, cutout_path, image_path, created_at",
32	    )
33	    .eq("archived", false)
34	    .order("created_at", { ascending: false });
35	  if (filters.slot) query = query.eq("slot", filters.slot);
36	  if (filters.season) query = query.contains("seasons", [filters.season]);
37	  if (filters.q) {
38	    const term = filters.q.replace(/[%,()]/g, " ").trim();
39	    if (term) query = query.or(`category.ilike.%${term}%,subcategory.ilike.%${term}%`);
40	  }
41	  const { data, error } = await query;
42	  if (error) throw new Error(error.message);
43	
44	  const rows = data ?? [];
45	  const displayPath = (r: (typeof rows)[number]) => r.cutout_path ?? r.thumb_path ?? r.image_path;
46	  const paths = rows.map(displayPath);
47	  const urlByPath = new Map<string, string>();
48	  if (paths.length) {
49	    const { data: signed } = await supabase.storage
50	      .from(WARDROBE_BUCKET)
51	      .createSignedUrls(paths, SIGNED_URL_TTL_S);
52	    signed?.forEach((s) => s.path && s.signedUrl && urlByPath.set(s.path, s.signedUrl));
53	  }
54	  return rows.map((r) => ({ ...r, thumb_url: urlByPath.get(displayPath(r)) ?? null }));
55	}

Write: /home/palak_raisinghani/my/courses/Fashion_Assist/src/lib/styling/thumbBackdrop.ts
// A thumbnail's cut-out has a transparent background, shown inside `.lightbox`, whose own background is a
// dark gradient (see globals.css). A dark garment (black, navy, charcoal) on that dark gradient has almost no
// contrast and can read as invisible. This picks a warm, cloth-like neutral backdrop for dark garments only;
// light and mid-tone garments already read fine against the default dark background, so they keep it.
import { hexRgb, srgbToLab } from "./colourPair";
import type { Color } from "./types";

/** Below this Lab lightness (0-100) a garment is dark enough to risk vanishing into the default backdrop. */
const DARK_THRESHOLD = 32;
/** A soft, warm linen tone: close to cloth, not a stark white that would clash with the app's dark theme. */
const NEUTRAL_BACKDROP = "#ded7c7";

/** The thumbnail backdrop colour for a garment's colours, or undefined to keep the default (CSS) background. */
export function thumbBackdrop(colors: Color[] | null | undefined): string | undefined {
  const primary = (colors ?? []).find((c) => c.role === "primary") ?? colors?.[0];
  if (!primary) return undefined;
  const [lightness] = srgbToLab(hexRgb(primary.hex));
  return lightness < DARK_THRESHOLD ? NEUTRAL_BACKDROP : undefined;
}

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { thumbBackdrop } from "@/lib/styling/thumbBackdrop";

const c = (hex: string, role: "primary" | "secondary" = "primary") => ({ name: hex, hex, role });

describe("thumbBackdrop", () => {
  it("gives dark garments a neutral backdrop", () => {
    expect(thumbBackdrop([c("#000000")])).toBe("#ded7c7");
    expect(thumbBackdrop([c("#0a0a12")])).toBe("#ded7c7"); // near-black navy
  });
  it("leaves light and mid-tone garments alone (undefined = default background)", () => {
    expect(thumbBackdrop([c("#ffffff")])).toBeUndefined();
    expect(thumbBackdrop([c("#a8284f")])).toBeUndefined(); // mid-tone red
  });
  it("prefers the primary colour over others, and falls back to the first when none is marked primary", () => {
    expect(thumbBackdrop([c("#ffffff", "secondary"), c("#000000", "primary")])).toBe("#ded7c7");
    expect(thumbBackdrop([c("#000000", "secondary")])).toBe("#ded7c7");
  });
  it("is undefined with no colours", () => {
    expect(thumbBackdrop([])).toBeUndefined();
    expect(thumbBackdrop(null)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(thumbBackdrop(undefined)).toBeUndefined();
  });
});

Edit: /home/palak_raisinghani/my/courses/Fashion_Assist/DECISIONS.md
--- old
- **Not done:** outerwear pairs still fall back to the hand rule's `proportionScore` only, since outerwear bottoms don't exist and the bridge only covers top/bottom. `silhouette_matches` on `StyledItem` is a free slot for a future CLIP-based 4a to fill in; until then the bridge computes it on every call (cheap: no network, a fixed table scan over <=220 silhouettes).
+++ new
- **Not done:** outerwear pairs still fall back to the hand rule's `proportionScore` only, since outerwear bottoms don't exist and the bridge only covers top/bottom. `silhouette_matches` on `StyledItem` is a free slot for a future CLIP-based 4a to fill in; until then the bridge computes it on every call (cheap: no network, a fixed table scan over <=220 silhouettes).

## Garment -> silhouette matcher (4a) made live: a Python subprocess, backfilled onto the demo account (2026-10-25/26)
- **Why:** 4a was trained (see above) but never called; `pairScore` only ever saw the attribute bridge. The user asked to close that gap and see it working on the demo account.
- **How** (`experiments/silhouette-match/match_one.py`, `src/lib/ai/silhouetteMatch.ts`): there is no CLIP implementation anywhere in this app (checked: no transformers.js/onnx, no prior child_process precedent in `src/`), and no deployment config (no vercel.json/Dockerfile) suggesting a serverless target that would rule out shelling out to Python. Given tagging already waits seconds on a vision API call, a few more seconds for a Python subprocess (reusing the exact trained `head_v1.npz` and `features.py`, no reimplementation risk) was judged simpler and safer than adding a JS ML stack. The tag route calls it from its existing `after()` background callback, only for top/bottom/outerwear items with a cutout, and writes `items.silhouette_matches` (new nullable jsonb column, migration `20260101000010`) only when the matcher returns something; failures leave it null so a later retry can still succeed.
- **Preprocessing:** the live cut-out (`@imgly/background-removal`, transparent PNG) is composited onto white and masked from alpha >= 128, matching how the training images were prepared (confirmed via `colour-extract.ts`'s own alpha-based mask convention).
- **pairScore.ts:** an explicitly empty match array (`[]`, meaning the matcher ran but found nothing confident) now falls back to the bridge too, not just `null`/`undefined` — otherwise a legitimate "no match" result would permanently disable the model for that item instead of degrading to the heuristic.
- **Backfilled** the demo account's 5 pre-existing tagged items (`scripts/backfill-silhouette-matches.mjs`, re-runnable, only touches items where `silhouette_matches` is still null). Confidence scores came back low (0.10-0.28, vs 0.93 on a synthetic same-drawing sanity check) and one top-1 looked questionable (wide-leg palazzo pants -> a skirt silhouette, with the correct pants silhouette ranked second). Given only 5 real samples and no ground truth for them, this is not enough to say the live accuracy falls short of the 80.9%/95.5% cross-validated numbers — flagged to the user rather than asserted either way; a visual comparison page was generated locally (git-ignored, embeds real photos, never committed) so the user could judge by eye.

## Upload review: box/frame misalignment, then overlap + hard-to-toggle (2026-10-26)
- **Why:** uploading several photos in one batch showed boxes misaligned on the photo, and after that was fixed, overlapping transparent boxes were still hard to read and hard to tap the right one.
- **Misalignment** (`src/components/garment-splitter.tsx`): the photo `<img>` used `w-full object-contain` under a `max-h-[60vh]` cap. Whenever the cap applied (any portrait photo, i.e. most phone photos), the img's CSS box no longer matched its own aspect ratio, so `object-contain` letterboxed it — but the detection boxes are positioned as percentages of the *wrapping frame*, not the letterboxed content area, so they landed in the blank

  1. Overlapping transparent boxes / hard-to-toggle (garment-splitter.tsx): boxes are now outline-only and never intercept taps; each garment gets a small fixed-size badge (✓/✗ + number) anchored at its corner as the actual toggle — always easy to hit regardless of box size or overlap.

  3. Both pass typecheck/lint/tests (255/255), and are picked up by the running dev server via hot-reload.

79	export function normalizeUtilities(list: readonly Utility[]): Utility[] {
80	  const [main, ...rest] = [...new Set(list)];
81	  if (!main) return [];

10	] as const;

12	const isWhole = (s: Slot) => (WHOLE as readonly string[]).includes(s);
13	
14	/** Slots that make up the base of an outfit (garments). */
15	export const BASE_SLOTS: readonly Slot[] = [...BODY, ...WHOLE];
16	
17	/**
18	 * Whether two slots can appear together in one outfit.
19	 * A dress/onepiece excludes separate top/bottom; two items never share a slot.
20	 */
21	export function slotsCompatible(a: Slot, b: Slot): boolean {
22	  if (a === b) return false;
23	  if (isWhole(a) && (BODY as readonly string[]).includes(b)) return false;
24	  if (isWhole(b) && (BODY as readonly string[]).includes(a)) return false;
25	  if (isWhole(a) && isWhole(b)) return false;
26	  if (a === "outerwear" && b === "outerwear") return false;
27	  return true;
28	}
29	
30	/** Slot pairs worth scoring: everything compatible except jewellery-with-jewellery and accessory-with-jewellery
31	 *  (those are judged at whole-outfit level by set penalties, not pairwise). */
32	export function isScoredSlotPair(a: Slot, b: Slot): boolean {
33	  if (!slotsCompatible(a, b)) return false;
34	  if (isJewellery(a) && isJewellery(b)) return false;
35	  return true;
36	}
37	
38	export { isJewellery, isWhole };

42	  dress: {
43	    required: ["shoes", "bag", "jewellery_ear"],
44	    optional: ["jewellery_neck", "jewellery_wrist", "outerwear", "accessory"],
45	  },
46	  onepiece: {
47	    required: ["shoes", "jewellery_ear", "jewellery_neck"],
48	    optional: ["bag", "jewellery_wrist", "jewellery_other", "outerwear"],
49	  },
50	  top: {
51	    required: ["bottom", "shoes"],
52	    optional: ["bag", "jewellery_ear", "outerwear", "accessory"],
53	  },
54	  bottom: { required: ["top", "shoes"], optional: ["bag", "jewellery_ear", "outerwear"] },
55	  outerwear: { required: ["top", "bottom", "shoes"], optional: ["bag"] },
56	  shoes: { required: ["bag"], optional: ["jewellery_ear"] }, // plus (top+bottom) or dress; see planSlots
57	};
58	
59	export function planSlots(
60	  anchor: Slot,
61	  opts: { needsOuterwear?: boolean; hasDressLike?: boolean } = {},
62	): { required: Slot[]; optional: Slot[] } {
63	  let plan: { required: Slot[]; optional: Slot[] };
64	  if (anchor === "shoes") {
65	    const base: Slot[] = opts.hasDressLike ? ["dress"] : ["top", "bottom"];
66	    plan = { required: [...base, "bag"], optional: ["jewellery_ear"] };
67	  } else if (isJewellery(anchor)) {
68	    plan = { required: ["top", "bottom", "shoes"], optional: ["bag"] }; // or a dress/onepiece; callers choose
69	  } else {
70	    const p = SLOT_PLAN[anchor];
71	    plan = p
72	      ? { required: [...p.required], optional: [...p.optional] }
73	      : { required: [], optional: [] };
74	  }
75	  if (opts.needsOuterwear && !plan.required.includes("outerwear") && anchor !== "outerwear") {
76	    plan.required.push("outerwear");
77	    plan.optional = plan.optional.filter((s) => s !== "outerwear");
78	  }
79	  return plan;
80	}

const admin = createClient(url, key, { auth: { persistSession: false, autoRefreshToken: false } });

  .in("id", ids)
  .select("id, slot, category, subcategory");
console.log(error ? `ERROR: ${error.message}` : JSON.stringify(data, null, 1));

/** The shared demo account for reviewers: one password, and a token budget that stops runaway spend. Server-side only. */

const num = (v: string | undefined, fallback: number) => {
  const n = Number(v);
  return v !== undefined && v !== "" && Number.isFinite(n) ? n : fallback;
};

/** Supabase refuses passwords under this length, so the gate password can also be the account's own password. */
export const MIN_PASSWORD = 6;

export const DEFAULT_DEMO_PASSWORD = "fashion2rock";

/**
 * What a visitor types (the login page submits it) AND the demo account's real Supabase password: with a password of at
 * least MIN_PASSWORD characters there is no reason for them to differ.
 */
export const demoPassword = () => process.env.DEMO_PASSWORD || DEFAULT_DEMO_PASSWORD;

/**
 * Token budget of the demo account (input + output, all model calls). A tagging call costs roughly 2,500-4,000 tokens, so
 * the daily default is around 50-80 photos a day across every visitor. Either cap is off when set to 0: the lifetime cap
 * is off by default, because once spent it would kill the demo permanently rather than until tomorrow.
 */
export const demoTokenLimits = () => ({
  daily: num(process.env.DEMO_DAILY_TOKENS, 200_000),
  total: num(process.env.DEMO_TOTAL_TOKENS, 0),
});

/** Which budget, if any, is used up. A call that starts under the budget may overshoot it by that one call. */
export function demoBudgetState(
  usedToday: number,
  usedTotal: number,
  limits = demoTokenLimits(),
): "daily" | "total" | null {
  if (limits.total > 0 && usedTotal >= limits.total) return "total";
  if (limits.daily > 0 && usedToday >= limits.daily) return "daily";
  return null;
}

import { timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";
import { NextResponse, type NextRequest } from "next/server";
import { demoPassword } from "@/lib/demo";
import { createClient } from "@/lib/supabase/server";

function same(a: string, b: string) {
  const x = Buffer.from(a);
  const y = Buffer.from(b);
  return x.length === y.length && timingSafeEqual(x, y);
}

/** Password sign-in for the shared demo account (reviewers). Off unless DEMO_EMAIL is set; see DEMO_PASSWORD. */
export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
  const { origin } = new URL(request.url);
  const email = process.env.DEMO_EMAIL;
  if (!email) return NextResponse.redirect(`${origin}/login`, 303);

  const password = demoPassword();
  const given = String((await request.formData()).get("password") ?? "");
  if (!same(given, password)) return NextResponse.redirect(`${origin}/login?error=demo`, 303);

  const supabase = await createClient();
  const { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithPassword({ email, password });
  if (error) return NextResponse.redirect(`${origin}/login?error=demo`, 303);
  return NextResponse.redirect(`${origin}/closet`, 303);
}

/** Which budget, if any, is used up. A call that starts under the budget may overshoot it by that one call. */
export function demoBudgetState(
  usedToday: number,
  usedTotal: number,
  limits = demoTokenLimits(),
): "daily" | "total" | null {

/**
 * Whether a signed-in email is the shared demo account. Used to gate dev-only tooling (the per-item pipeline
 * debug view) to that one account, so it never shows up for a real user. False when DEMO_EMAIL is not set.
 */
export function isDemoEmail(email: string | null | undefined): boolean {
  const demoEmail = process.env.DEMO_EMAIL?.toLowerCase();
  return !!demoEmail && email?.toLowerCase() === demoEmail;
}

import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from "next/server";
import { createClient } from "@/lib/supabase/server";
import { isDemoEmail } from "@/lib/demo";
import { silhouetteById } from "@/lib/styling/silhouettes";

/**
 * Serves a library silhouette's reference drawing from local disk (datasets/silhouettes/library/), for the
 * demo-only pipeline debug view (see /style/[itemId]/debug). These pictures are never in the `public/`
 * folder and are otherwise only read by the offline Python tools, so this is the one place the running app
 * reads them; gated the same way as the debug page itself, even though the pictures are not sensitive.
 */
export async function GET(_req: NextRequest, { params }: { params: Promise<{ id: string }> }) {
  const supabase = await createClient();
  const {
    data: { user },
  } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
  if (!isDemoEmail(user?.email)) return new NextResponse(null, { status: 404 });

  const { id } = await params;
  const sil = silhouetteById(id);
  if (!sil) return new NextResponse(null, { status: 404 });

  const root = process.cwd();
  const clean = path.join(root, sil.image.replace(/\.png$/, "_clean.png"));
  const plain = path.join(root, sil.image);
  const file = await readFile(clean).catch(() => readFile(plain).catch(() => null));
  if (!file) return new NextResponse(null, { status: 404 });
  return new NextResponse(file, { headers: { "content-type": "image/png" } });
}

/** A plain key/value row; value is JSON-stringified when it's not already a readable string or number. */
function Row({ label, value }: { label: string; value: unknown }) {
  if (value === null || value === undefined) return null;
  const text =
    typeof value === "string" || typeof value === "number"
      ? String(value)
      : Array.isArray(value) && value.every((v) => typeof v === "string")
        ? value.join(", ")
        : JSON.stringify(value);
  if (!text || text === "[]" || text === "{}") return null;
  return (
    <div className="flex items-start justify-between gap-3 border-b border-[var(--line)] py-1.5 text-sm last:border-0">
      <span className="muted shrink-0">{label}</span>
      <span className="text-right break-words">{text}</span>
    </div>
  );
}

## Dark garments were invisible in the closet (2026-10-26)
- **Why:** a cut-out's background is transparent; `.lightbox`'s own background is a dark gradient (`#2b2b35` to `#15151c`). A black, navy or charcoal garment has almost no contrast against that and effectively disappears.
- **How** (`src/lib/styling/thumbBackdrop.ts`): a pure function reusing `colourPair.ts`'s existing Lab conversion — below Lab lightness 32 (both thresholds picked by eye, not derived from data), swap the thumbnail's backdrop to a warm neutral `#ded7c7` (evoking cloth/linen, not a stark white that would clash with the app's dark theme); lighter garments keep the default background unchanged. Wired through `listItems` (`ItemRow.thumb_backdrop`, needs the `colors` column already on `items`) into `Rail` (`RailItem.backdrop`, an inline style override) and the closet's own 2-column grid view.
- **Scoped to the closet only** (`/closet`), since that is what was asked; `Rail` is also used on `/style` and the item spotlight page, but those are fed by `MatchItem` (`src/lib/matches.ts`), which does not carry colour data yet — extending there would need `colors` added to `ITEM_COLS`/`MatchItem`, not done here.
