## "Ethnic sets" (onepiece) removed from the taxonomy (user decision, 2026-10-26)
- **Why:** the user asked why the closet showed an "Ethnic sets" rail. It was not a bug — the demo account genuinely had a kurta set and a co-ord set, both correctly tagged under `onepiece` per `CATEGORIES_BY_SLOT`. `SPECFashion.md:311` explicitly calls regional/ethnic wear a deliberate differentiator ("included from day one"), so removing the slot is a real spec deviation — flagged to the user before acting; they confirmed removing it entirely rather than archiving/hiding.

The tagger prompt now folds sarees, lehengas, anarkalis, kurta sets and co-ord sets into `slot dress`, with `jumpsuit` as the fallback category when nothing else fits — bumped `tagger.v11` -> `tagger.v12` since this changes tagging behaviour (CLAUDE.md rule: bump the version on any prompt change). `docs/TAGGER.md` regenerated (`python3 scripts/gen_tagger_doc.py`).
- **The 2 existing items were retagged** (`slot: dress, category: jumpsuit`), not archived or deleted: their actual data (photos, colours, subcategory text) is untouched, and this keeps them usable/matchable rather than disappearing from the closet — judged as the better fit for "we don't need that *section*" than silently hiding real wardrobe items. No data was deleted (standing rule).
- All ~20 touched call sites and test fixtures (tests referencing `onepiece`/`saree`/`kurta_set` as a slot or category) updated to use `dress`/`jumpsuit` instead; full list in the commit diff. 256/256 tests pass.

--- old
- Library silhouette pictures live under `datasets/silhouettes/library/`, never in `public/`, and are otherwise only read by offline Python tools — added `/api/debug/silhouette-image/[id]` to serve them from disk for this one view, gated by the same `isDemoEmail` check (defense in depth; the pictures themselves are not sensitive).
+++ new
- Library silhouette pictures live under `datasets/silhouettes/library/`, never in `public/`, and are otherwise only read by offline Python tools — added `/api/debug/silhouette-image/[id]` to serve them from disk for this one view, gated by the same `isDemoEmail` check (defense in depth; the pictures themselves are not sensitive).

## Closet slot tabs lost the scrollable hanger rail (2026-10-26)
- **Why:** `/closet`'s "All" view shows one horizontally-scrollable `Rail` per slot, but clicking a specific tab (Tops, Bottoms, ...) switched to a static 2-column grid instead — the `filtered` flag covered both a slot filter and a text search, and only the grid branch existed for either.
- **How** (`closet/page.tsx`): split the two cases. A slot-only filter now renders a single `Rail` (still scrollable, title derived from `SLOT_LABELS`, falling back to the raw slot string for an invalid/stale `?slot=` value instead of printing "undefined"). A text search (`?q=`, with or without a slot) keeps the grid, since results can span several slots and a grid reads better there. Reused `items` (already filtered server-side by `listItems`) rather than re-deriving from `all`.

# Closet — working rules

Follow SPEC.md (SPECFashion.md in this repo). Work one milestone at a time (Section 14). Do not start a
milestone until the previous one's acceptance criteria pass. Commit after each milestone (`M3: tagger + review UI`).

1. If something is ambiguous, choose the simplest option satisfying the spec and note it in `DECISIONS.md`.
2. Run typecheck, lint, tests, and the relevant eval before declaring a milestone done.

Bash: Build a contact sheet of clean labelled garment cut-outs
cd /home/palak_raisinghani/my/courses/Fashion_Assist && experiments/embeddings/.venv/bin/python -I - <<'EOF'
import json
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
root = "datasets/silhouette-match/"
pool = {p["id"]: p for p in json.load(open(root + "pool/pool.json"))}
lab = {json.loads(l)["id"]: json.loads(l) for l in open(root + "labels.jsonl") if l.strip()}
ids = [i for i, r in lab.items() if not r.get("bad") and not r.get("none") and not i.startswith("web_") and i in pool]
ids.sort(key=lambda i: (not i.startswith("tt_"), pool[i]["slot"], i))
ids = ids[:60]
W, H, cols = 150, 190, 10
sheet = Image.new("RGB", (cols * W, ((len(ids) + cols - 1) // cols) * H), "white")
d = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
for n, i in enumerate(ids):
    im = Image.open(root + f"pool/{i}_cut.png").convert("RGBA")
    bg = Image.new("RGB", im.size, "white"); bg.paste(im, (0, 0), im); im = bg
    im.thumbnail((W - 10, H - 30))
    x, y = (n % cols) * W, (n // cols) * H
    sheet.paste(im, (x + 5, y + 5))
    d.text((x + 3, y + H - 22), f"{n}:{i[:18]}", fill="black")
sheet.save("/tmp/claude-1001/-home-palak-raisinghani-my-courses-Fashion-Assist/a621cbb1-b24f-4361-a8a3-0608d4c8e9bf/scratchpad/pitch_contact.jpg", quality=80)
json.dump(ids, open("/tmp/claude-1001/-home-palak-raisinghani-my-courses-Fashion-Assist/a621cbb1-b24f-4361-a8a3-0608d4c8e9bf/scratchpad/pitch_contact.json", "w"))
print(len(ids))
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the images and data for the Fashion Aina product pitch (product-pitch/).

Usage: ../embeddings/.venv/bin/python -I build.py [--epochs 80]
Writes product-pitch/assets/img/* (WebP, resized), product-pitch/assets/fonts/*, product-pitch/assets/data.js.
The page itself (index.html, style.css, app.js) is hand-written; this only refreshes what it shows. Everything lands
inside product-pitch/ so the folder can be copied anywhere (GitHub Pages) with no outside links.

The garment -> silhouette examples are honest: the matcher is retrained once with every showcased garment (and the
other photo of the same product) held out, so each prediction shown comes from a model that never saw that garment.
"""
import argparse, json, shutil, sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[1]
OUT = ROOT / "product-pitch"
IMG = OUT / "assets" / "img"
DS = ROOT / "datasets"
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "experiments" / "silhouette-match"))

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=80)
args = ap.parse_args()

for d in ("photos", "garments", "cutouts", "sil", "pairs", "colourpairs"):
    (IMG / d).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
(OUT / "assets" / "fonts").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
for f in (ROOT / "public" / "fonts").glob("cmu-serif-*.woff2"):
    shutil.copy(f, OUT / "assets" / "fonts" / f.name)


def save(im, path, max_h, q=82, max_w=None):
    im = im.copy()
    im.thumbnail((max_w or max_h * 3, max_h), Image.LANCZOS)
    im.save(path, "WEBP", quality=q, method=6)
    return {"w": im.width, "h": im.height}


def rel(p):
    return str(p.relative_to(OUT))


LIB = json.load(open(ROOT / "src/lib/styling/silhouettes.json"))
LIB_BY = {s["id"]: s for s in LIB}


def sil_img(sid):
    """The library drawing, small, as WebP (cached)."""
    dst = IMG / "sil" / f"{sid}.webp"
    if not dst.exists():
        src = DS / "silhouettes" / "library" / f"{sid}_clean.png"
        if not src.exists():
            src = DS / "silhouettes" / "library" / f"{sid}.png"
        save(Image.open(src).convert("RGB"), dst, 200, q=80)
    return rel(dst)


data = {}

# ---- 1. segmentation + tagging: the playground set ----------------------------------------------------------------
tt = DS / "tagger-test"
boxes = json.load(open(tt / "boxes.json"))
tags = json.load(open(tt / "claude-tags.json"))
garm_meta = json.load(open(tt / "garments.json"))
photos = []
for photo, bs in boxes.items():
    stem = photo.rsplit(".", 1)[0]
    size = save(Image.open(tt / photo).convert("RGB"), IMG / "photos" / f"{stem}.webp", 760, q=80)
    garments = []
    for b in bs:
        name = f"{stem}__{b['id']}"
        crop_p, mask_p = tt / "garments" / f"{name}.jpg", tt / "_mask" / f"{name}.png"
        if not crop_p.exists():
            continue
        crop = Image.open(crop_p).convert("RGB")
        save(crop, IMG / "garments" / f"{name}.webp", 300, q=80)
        cut = None
        if mask_p.exists():
            mask = Image.open(mask_p).convert("L").resize(crop.size)
            rgba = crop.convert("RGBA")
            rgba.putalpha(mask)
            bbox = mask.point(lambda v: 255 if v > 127 else 0).getbbox()
            if bbox:
                rgba = rgba.crop(bbox)
            save(rgba, IMG / "cutouts" / f"tt_{name}.webp", 300, q=82)
            cut = f"assets/img/cutouts/tt_{name}.webp"
        t = tags.get(f"{name}.jpg", {})
        pal = (garm_meta.get(f"{name}.jpg") or {}).get("palette") or []
        garments.append({
            "id": b["id"], "hint": b.get("hint"), "box": b["box"],
            "crop": f"assets/img/garments/{name}.webp", "cutout": cut,
            "palette": [{"hex": p["hex"], "share": p["share"]} for p in pal],
            "tags": {k: t.get(k) for k in ("subcategory", "slot", "category", "colors", "pattern", "fabric", "formality",

def rel(p):
    return str(p.relative_to(OUT))


POOL = DS / "silhouette-match" / "pool"


def pool_cutout(gid):
    """A pool garment with a transparent background: the cut-out is stored on white, its mask alongside it."""
    cut, mask_p = POOL / f"{gid}_cut.png", POOL / f"{gid}_mask.png"
    if not cut.exists() or not mask_p.exists():
        return None
    im = Image.open(cut).convert("RGBA")
    mask = Image.open(mask_p).convert("L").resize(im.size)
    im.putalpha(mask)
    bbox = mask.point(lambda v: 255 if v > 127 else 0).getbbox()
    save(im.crop(bbox) if bbox else im, IMG / "cutouts" / f"{gid}.webp", 300, q=82)
    return f"assets/img/cutouts/{gid}.webp"

/* Fashion Aina — product pitch. Same identity as the app: near-black with a purple cast, a purple / pink / blue
   gradient, Computer Modern for headlines. Charts use the system sans and colours validated for this dark surface. */

@font-face {
  font-family: "CMU Serif";
  src: url("fonts/cmu-serif-500-roman.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight: 400 500;
  font-style: normal;
  font-display: swap;
}
@font-face {
  font-family: "CMU Serif";
  src: url("fonts/cmu-serif-700-roman.woff2") format("woff2");

  font-style: normal;
  font-display: swap;
}
@font-face {
  font-family: "CMU Serif";
  src: url("fonts/cmu-serif-500-italic.woff2") format("woff2");

  font-style: italic;
  font-display: swap;
}

:root {
  color-scheme: dark;
  --bg: #07070b;
  --surface: #0f0f16;
  --card: #14141c;
  --card-2: #1a1a24;
  --line: #262633;
  --line-2: #33333f;
  --ink: #f3f1f7;
  --ink-2: #c4c0d0;
  --muted: #8e8a99;

  --purple: #a14bff;
  --pink: #e42278;
  --blue: #3987e5;
  --blue-brand: #116dff;
  --aqua: #199e70;
  --amber: #c98500;
  --light: #b9aee6;
  --glow: rgb(161 75 255 / 0.22);
  --grad: linear-gradient(100deg, #a14bff, #e42278 50%, #116dff);

  /* garment light box: a lit warm neutral, so a garment of any colour reads (the app uses the same idea) */
  --lightbox: #ece8df;

  /* stage families (validated order on --card: aqua, purple, amber, blue, pink) */
  --f-vision: var(--aqua);
  --f-lm: var(--purple);
  --f-colour: var(--amber);
  --f-shape: var(--blue);
  --f-score: var(--pink);

  --serif: "CMU Serif", ui-serif, Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif;
  --sans: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;

}

  box-sizing: border-box;
}

  scroll-behavior: smooth;
  scroll-padding-top: 72px;
}

  overflow-x: hidden;
}

  max-width: 100%;
  display: block;
}
a {
  color: inherit;
}

  font: inherit;
  color: inherit;
}

}

.wrap {

/* Fashion Aina - product pitch. Renders everything from window.AINA (assets/data.js, built by
   experiments/pitch/build.py). No libraries, no network: the folder works wherever it is copied. */
(() => {
  "use strict";
  const D = window.AINA;
  const S = D.stats;
  const $ = (s, r = document) => r.querySelector(s);
  const esc = (s) =>
    String(s ?? "").replace(/[&<>"']/g, (c) => ({ "&": "&amp;", "<": "&lt;", ">": "&gt;", '"': "&quot;", "'": "&#39;" })[c]);
  const pretty = (s) => String(s ?? "").replace(/_/g, " ");
  const num = (n) => Number(n).toLocaleString("en-GB");
  const libBy = Object.fromEntries(D.library.map((s) => [s.id, s]));

  // colours: stage families (validated on the card surface: aqua, purple, amber, blue, pink), chart series, chrome
  const FAM = { vision: "#199e70", lm: "#a14bff", colour: "#c98500", shape: "#3987e5", score: "#e42278" };
  const SERIES = ["#a14bff", "#e42278"]; // a validated pair on the dark card
  const INK = "#f3f1f7", INK2 = "#c4c0d0", MUTED = "#8e8a99", GRID = "#262633", AXIS = "#4a4a58";

  const img = (src, alt = "", cls = "") =>
    `<img src="${esc(src)}" alt="${esc(alt)}" loading="lazy" decoding="async"${cls ? ` class="${cls}"` : ""}>`;

  /* ---------------------------------------------------------------- tooltip */
  const tip = $("#tip");
  function showTip(html, e) {
    tip.innerHTML = html;
    tip.classList.add("show");
    moveTip(e);
  }
  function moveTip(e) {
    const pad = 14;
    const r = tip.getBoundingClientRect();
    let x = e.clientX + pad, y = e.clientY + pad;
    if (x + r.width > innerWidth - 8) x = e.clientX - r.width - pad;
    if (y + r.height > innerHeight - 8) y = e.clientY - r.height - pad;
    tip.style.left = `${Math.max(8, x)}px`;
    tip.style.top = `${Math.max(8, y)}px`;
  }
  const hideTip = () => tip.classList.remove("show");

  /* ---------------------------------------------------------------- shared bits */
  const boxStyle = (b) =>
    `left:${b[0] * 100}%;top:${b[1] * 100}%;width:${(b[2] - b[0]) * 100}%;height:${(b[3] - b[1]) * 100}%`;
  const stars = (r) => {
    const full = Math.round(r);
    return `<span class="stars" aria-label="${r} out of 5">${"★".repeat(full)}<span class="off">${"★".repeat(5 - full)}</span></span>`;
  };
  const dots = (v, max = 5) =>
    `<span class="dots" aria-label="${v ?? "?"} of ${max}">${Array.from({ length: max }, (_, i) => `<i class="${i < (v || 0) ? "on" : ""}"></i>`).join("")}</span>`;
  const table = (head, rows) =>
    `<details class="table"><summary>View as table</summary><div class="table-scroll"><table><thead><tr>${head
      .map((h) => `<th>${esc(h)}</th>`)
      .join("")}</tr></thead><tbody>${rows
      .map((r) => `<tr>${r.map((c) => `<td>${esc(c)}</td>`).join("")}</tr>`)
      .join("")}</tbody></table></div></details>`;

  /* ---------------------------------------------------------------- hero */
  function hero() {
    const p = D.photos.find((x) => x.id === "1-718144534") || D.photos[0];
    const kept = p.garments.filter((g) => g.cutout);
    const sil = ["shirt_classic_shirt", "pants_wide_leg_pants"].map((id) => libBy[id]).filter(Boolean);
    $("#journey").innerHTML = `
      <figure>
        <div class="photo">${img(p.src, "A street-style photo from the playground set")}
          ${p.garments.map((g) => `<div class="box" style="${boxStyle(g.box)};cursor:default"><span>${esc(pretty(g.id))}</span></div>`).join("")}
        </div>
        <figcaption>Photo</figcaption>
      </figure>
      <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">&rarr;</div>

--- old
/* heatmap */
+++ new
/* horizontal bars (long labels) */
.hbars {
  position: relative;
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 260px) minmax(0, 1fr);
  column-gap: 14px;
  row-gap: 8px;
  align-items: center;
}
@media (max-width: 560px) {
  .hbars {
    grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 130px) minmax(0, 1fr);
  }
}
.hlabel {
  font-size: 0.86rem;
  color: var(--ink-2);
  text-align: right;
  line-height: 1.25;
}
.htrack {
  position: relative;
  height: 24px;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 8px;
  cursor: default;
}
.hbar {
  height: 18px;
  border-radius: 0 4px 4px 0;
  min-width: 2px;
}
.hval {
  font-size: 0.8rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  color: var(--ink-2);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
}
.chart:hover .htrack:not(:hover) .hbar {
  opacity: 0.55;
}
.href {
  position: absolute;
  top: -6px;
  bottom: -6px;
  grid-column: 2;
  border-left: 1.5px dashed var(--ink-2);
  opacity: 0.85;
  pointer-events: none;
}
.hbars .href {
  /* placed in the track column: offset by the label column + gap */
  margin-left: calc(var(--label-col, 260px) + 14px);
}
.href span {
  position: absolute;
  bottom: 100%;
  left: 6px;
  font-size: 0.74rem;
  color: var(--ink-2);
  white-space: nowrap;
}

// Drives the pitch page in headless Chromium over CDP: clicks, reads results, reports exceptions and overflow.
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { setTimeout as sleep } from "node:timers/promises";

const [width, height] = (process.argv[2] || "1280x900").split("x").map(Number);
const url = `file://${process.argv[3]}`;
const bin = `${process.env.HOME}/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1187/chrome-linux/headless_shell`;
const port = 9333 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 300);
const proc = spawn(bin, ["--no-sandbox", `--remote-debugging-port=${port}`, `--window-size=${width},${height}`, "about:blank"], { stdio: "ignore" });

let ws;
for (let i = 0; i < 40 && !ws; i++) {
  await sleep(150);
  try {
    const list = await (await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}/json`)).json();
    const page = list.find((t) => t.type === "page");
    if (page) ws = new WebSocket(page.webSocketDebuggerUrl);
  } catch {}
}
await new Promise((r) => (ws.onopen = r));
let id = 0;
const pending = new Map();
const errors = [];
ws.onmessage = (m) => {
  const msg = JSON.parse(m.data);
  if (msg.id && pending.has(msg.id)) pending.get(msg.id)(msg.result);
  if (msg.method === "Runtime.exceptionThrown") errors.push(msg.params.exceptionDetails.exception?.description || msg.params.exceptionDetails.text);
  if (msg.method === "Runtime.consoleAPICalled" && msg.params.type === "error") errors.push(msg.params.args.map((a) => a.value).join(" "));
};
const send = (method, params = {}) => new Promise((r) => { const i = ++id; pending.set(i, r); ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id: i, method, params })); });
const ev = async (expr) => (await send("Runtime.evaluate", { expression: expr, returnByValue: true, awaitPromise: true })).result.value;

await send("Runtime.enable");
await send("Page.enable");
await send("Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride", { width, height, deviceScaleFactor: 1, mobile: width < 600 });
await send("Page.navigate", { url });
await sleep(1500);

## Product pitch page: a self-contained static site in product-pitch/ (2026-10-26)
- **What:** `product-pitch/index.html` explains the whole pipeline as a product pitch ("Fashion Aina"): flow graph, an interactive walk through the playground set (photo -> boxes -> crop -> cut-out -> tags -> measured palette), the colour model's taste matrix, the silhouette library, what a model reads off a silhouette, held-out garment -> silhouette matches, the silhouette-pair model's best and worst pairings, the scoring rules, and the design principles. Plain HTML/CSS/JS, no libraries and no network requests, so the folder can be copied as-is to GitHub Pages. Named `product-pitch` (not "product pitch") because a space in a URL path is fragile.
- **Images published (user's decision):** asked before building, since the repo is private and Pages is public. The user chose to include everything: the playground photos (third-party web images of people, one with a site watermark) and the silhouette library drawings (from third-party sheets). Not included: personal closet photos from the demo account (not offered) and the shop photos (`pool/web_*`, git-ignored).
- **Honest examples:** the 12 garment -> silhouette matches shown are from a matcher retrained once with those garments (and the other photo of the same product) held out - 10 of 12 have a human-labelled silhouette in the top 3, consistent with the 92.5% cross-validated top-3. The two misses are shown with the reason.
- **Rebuilt by** `experiments/pitch/build.py` (run with `../embeddings/.venv/bin/python -I build.py`): resizes images to WebP inside the folder and writes `assets/data.js`; the page reads only that. Chart colours were run through the dataviz palette validator against the page's dark surface (purple/pink for two series; aqua, purple, amber, blue, pink for the stage families; amber, blue, aqua, purple, pink for the weights bar).

29:- **Product pitch** (`product-pitch/`, self-contained static site for GitHub Pages): explains the pipeline with the playground images, the silhouette library and held-out match examples. Rebuild its images/data with `experiments/pitch/build.py`.

The Fashion Aina pitch page is built in product-pitch/. Everything it needs is inside the folder (2.8 MB, no outside links), so you can copy it straight into your GitHub Pages repo. Open product-pitch/index.html to preview it locally.

I named the folder product-pitch rather than "product pitch", because a space in a web address tends to break.

The page runs in this order: - Hero: a playground photo, then the garments found in it, then their matched silhouettes, with the headline numbers. - Flow graph: all 7 stages, colour-coded. Tapping a stage jumps to its section. - Find and Describe: pick any of the 9 playground photos and click a box or garment. You see the crop, the background-removed cut-out, every tag, and the colours the picker measured. - Colour: the colour model's predicted ratings for 10 wardrobe colours as a heat grid, examples of what you rated, and why the small network on perceptual colour won. - Shape: the full 220-drawing library with family filters, and what the model actually reads off a silhouette (its outline widths and a grid of where its lines are). - Match examples: 12 garments matched to silhouettes, plus the accuracy chart going from 62% to 95.5%. - Silhouette-pair model: what you rated, its accuracy, and its favourite and least-favourite pairings. - Scoring: the weights, the rules that can veto a pair, and how pairs go from rule score to vision ranker to the top 5. - Design decisions and the tech stack.

The 12 match examples come from a copy of the matcher retrained without those garments, so none of them were seen in training. 10 of 12 have one of your labelled silhouettes in the top 3; the 2 misses are shown with the reason.

As you chose, the page includes the playground photos and the library drawings. Both come from third-party sources and are now headed for a public site. Your personal closet photos and the shop photos are left out. This is recorded in DECISIONS.md.

I checked it in headless Chrome at desktop and phone width. All the clicks and hovers work, there are no errors, and nothing spills off the side on a phone.

If you change data, re-run experiments/pitch/build.py to refresh the page's images and numbers. Nothing is committed yet — want me to commit and push it?

import { z } from "zod";
import { callTool, currentProvider } from "@/lib/ai/client";
import { imageSeed } from "@/lib/ai/mock-tagger";
import { DETECT_PROMPT_VERSION, DETECT_SYSTEM, DETECT_USER_TEXT } from "@/lib/ai/prompts/detect.v1";
import { cleanDetections, MAX_DETECTIONS, type Detected } from "@/lib/upload/detections";

const edge = z.number().min(0).max(1000);

export const DetectResult = z.object({
  garments: z
    .array(
      z.object({
        label: z.string().max(60),
        box: z.object({ ymin: edge, xmin: edge, ymax: edge, xmax: edge }),
      }),
    )
    .max(MAX_DETECTIONS + 4),
});

/**
 * Finds the separate items in one photo and returns clean boxes (fractions of the photo, reading order).
 * An empty list means nothing was found; the caller falls back to the whole photo or manual boxes.
 */
export async function detectGarments(args: {
  userId: string;
  image: { mediaType: "image/jpeg"; base64: string };
}): Promise<{ garments: Detected[]; promptVersion: string; model: string }> {
  if (currentProvider() === "mock") {
    // A stable fake split so the review screen can be exercised without a model: top over bottom, or a single item.
    const two = imageSeed(args.image.base64) % 4 !== 0;
    const raw = two
      ? [
          { label: "top", box: { ymin: 60, xmin: 180, ymax: 480, xmax: 820 } },
          { label: "bottom", box: { ymin: 500, xmin: 220, ymax: 960, xmax: 780 } },
        ]
      : [{ label: "garment", box: { ymin: 80, xmin: 150, ymax: 940, xmax: 850 } }];
    return { garments: cleanDetections(raw), promptVersion: "mock.v0", model: "mock" };
  }
  const model = process.env.MODEL_DETECT || process.env.MODEL_TAGGER;
  if (!model) throw new Error("MODEL_TAGGER (or MODEL_DETECT) is not configured");
  const { data } = await callTool({
    userId: args.userId,
    purpose: "detect",
    model,
    promptVersion: DETECT_PROMPT_VERSION,
    system: DETECT_SYSTEM,
    userText: DETECT_USER_TEXT,
    images: [args.image],
    toolName: "record_garments",
    toolDescription: "Record a box and a short label for every wardrobe item in the photo.",
    schema: DetectResult,
    maxTokens: 900,
    timeoutMs: 20_000,
  });
  return { garments: cleanDetections(data.garments), promptVersion: DETECT_PROMPT_VERSION, model };
}

import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from "next/server";
import sharp from "sharp";
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { currentProvider } from "@/lib/ai/client";
import { tagImage } from "@/lib/ai/tagger";
import { flattenTags, playgroundEnabled } from "@/lib/playground";

export const maxDuration = 60;
const MAX_BYTES = 10 * 1024 * 1024;

/** Dev playground: tag one uploaded or pasted photo. No login, no database, nothing stored. */
export async function POST(req: NextRequest) {
  if (!playgroundEnabled()) return new NextResponse(null, { status: 404 });
  const form = await req.formData().catch(() => null);
  const file = form?.get("image");
  if (!(file instanceof File))
    return NextResponse.json({ ok: false, error: "No image" }, { status: 400 });
  if (file.size > MAX_BYTES)
    return NextResponse.json({ ok: false, error: "Image over 10 MB" }, { status: 413 });

  let jpeg: Buffer;
  try {
    // Same preparation as the app's upload pipeline: honour EXIF rotation, long side <= 1024, JPEG, metadata stripped.
    jpeg = await sharp(Buffer.from(await file.arrayBuffer()))
      .rotate()
      .resize(1024, 1024, { fit: "inside", withoutEnlargement: true })
      .jpeg({ quality: 85 })
      .toBuffer();
  } catch {
    return NextResponse.json({ ok: false, error: "Not a readable image" }, { status: 400 });
  }

  const started = Date.now();
  try {
    const { tags, promptVersion, model } = await tagImage({
      userId: "playground",
      image: { mediaType: "image/jpeg", base64: jpeg.toString("base64") },
      noLog: true,
    });
    return NextResponse.json({
      ok: true,
      data: {
        tags,
        rows: flattenTags(tags),
        promptVersion,
        model,
        provider: currentProvider(),
        latencyMs: Date.now() - started,
        imageHash: createHash("sha1").update(jpeg).digest("hex").slice(0, 16),
      },
    });
  } catch (e) {
    // Show the reason (missing key, quota, validation) but never anything about the image.
    const msg = e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Tagging failed";
    return NextResponse.json({ ok: false, error: msg }, { status: 502 });
  }
}

export type ToolCallOptions<T extends z.ZodType> = {
  userId: string;

  model: string;
  promptVersion: string;
  system: string;
  userText: string;
  images?: ImageInput[];
  toolName: string;
  toolDescription: string;
  schema: T;
  maxTokens?: number;
  timeoutMs?: number;
  /** Dev playground only: no spend-cap check and no llm_calls row (needs no database). */
  noLog?: boolean;
};

async function logCall(row: {
  noLog?: boolean;
  userId: string;
  purpose: LlmPurpose;
  model: string;
  promptVersion: string;
  inputTokens: number;
  outputTokens: number;
  latencyMs: number;
  ok: boolean;
  error?: string;
}) {
  if (row.noLog) return;
  // Never include image bytes or prompt text here.
  await createAdminClient()
    .from("llm_calls")
    .insert({
      user_id: row.userId,
      purpose: row.purpose,
      model: row.model,
      prompt_version: row.promptVersion,
      input_tokens: row.inputTokens,
      output_tokens: row.outputTokens,
      cost_usd: costUsd(row.model, row.inputTokens, row.outputTokens),
      latency_ms: row.latencyMs,
      ok: row.ok,
      error: row.error?.slice(0, 500),
    });
}

// Runs the app's own garment detector (detect.v1, same prompt, model, schema and clean-up as src/lib/ai/detector.ts)
// over the demo closet photos, for the product pitch. Run from the repo root:
//   npx tsx --env-file=.env.local experiments/pitch/detect.ts
// noLog mode, as the dev playground uses: no spend-cap check against the demo account and no llm_calls row.
// Results are cached in datasets/pitch/detections.json; a photo already there is not sent again.
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import sharp from "sharp";
import { callTool } from "@/lib/ai/client";
import { DetectResult } from "@/lib/ai/detector";
import { DETECT_PROMPT_VERSION, DETECT_SYSTEM, DETECT_USER_TEXT } from "@/lib/ai/prompts/detect.v1";
import { cleanDetections } from "@/lib/upload/detections";

const SRC = "demo_closet";
const OUT = "datasets/pitch/detections.json";
const DETECT_SIDE = 768; // as src/lib/upload/prepare.ts

mkdirSync(path.dirname(OUT), { recursive: true });
const cache: Record<string, unknown> = existsSync(OUT) ? JSON.parse(readFileSync(OUT, "utf8")) : {};
const model = process.env.MODEL_DETECT || process.env.MODEL_TAGGER;
if (!model) throw new Error("MODEL_TAGGER (or MODEL_DETECT) is not configured");

const files = readdirSync(SRC).filter((f) => !f.startsWith(".")).sort();
for (const f of files) {
  if (cache[f]) continue;
  const img = sharp(readFileSync(path.join(SRC, f))).rotate();
  const meta = await img.metadata();
  const jpeg = await img
    .resize(DETECT_SIDE, DETECT_SIDE, { fit: "inside", withoutEnlargement: true })
    .flatten({ background: "#ffffff" })
    .jpeg({ quality: 85 })
    .toBuffer();
  try {
    const { data } = await callTool({
      userId: "pitch-build",
      purpose: "detect",
      model,
      promptVersion: DETECT_PROMPT_VERSION,
      system: DETECT_SYSTEM,
      userText: DETECT_USER_TEXT,
      images: [{ mediaType: "image/jpeg", base64: jpeg.toString("base64") }],
      toolName: "record_garments",
      toolDescription: "Record a box and a short label for every wardrobe item in the photo.",
      schema: DetectResult,
      maxTokens: 900,
      timeoutMs: 30_000,
      noLog: true,
    });
    const garments = cleanDetections(data.garments);
    cache[f] = { width: meta.width, height: meta.height, model, promptVersion: DETECT_PROMPT_VERSION, garments };
    console.log(`${f}: ${garments.map((g) => g.label).join(", ") || "(nothing)"}`);
  } catch (e) {
    console.log(`${f}: FAILED ${e instanceof Error ? e.message : "unknown"}`);
  }
  writeFileSync(OUT, JSON.stringify(cache, null, 1));
}
console.log(`${Object.keys(cache).length}/${files.length} photos detected -> ${OUT}`);

// Exports the demo account's closet (the app pipeline's real outputs: box crop, cut-out, tags, colours, silhouette
// matches) for the product pitch. Run from the repo root:  node --env-file=.env.local experiments/pitch/export_demo.mjs
// Writes datasets/pitch/demo_items/<id>_orig.jpg, <id>_cut.png and datasets/pitch/demo_items.json. Read-only on the DB.
import { mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { createClient } from "@supabase/supabase-js";

const { NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: url, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY: key, DEMO_EMAIL } = process.env;
if (!url || !key || !DEMO_EMAIL) throw new Error("Set NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and DEMO_EMAIL");
const admin = createClient(url, key, { auth: { persistSession: false, autoRefreshToken: false } });
const { data: list } = await admin.auth.admin.listUsers({ perPage: 1000 });
const user = list.users.find((u) => u.email === DEMO_EMAIL);
const { data: items, error } = await admin
  .from("items")
  .select(
    "id, slot, category, subcategory, colors, pattern, pattern_detail, garment_detail, fabric, formality, warmth, seasons, neckline, statement_level, style_tags, occasions, fit, length, tagger_version, silhouette_matches, image_path, cutout_path, created_at",
  )
  .eq("user_id", user.id)
  .eq("archived", false)
  .neq("slot", "untagged")
  .order("created_at");
if (error) throw new Error(error.message);

const dir = "datasets/pitch/demo_items";
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
for (const it of items) {
  for (const [p, name] of [[it.image_path, "orig.jpg"], [it.cutout_path, "cut.png"]]) {
    if (!p) continue;
    const { data: blob } = await admin.storage.from("wardrobe").download(p);
    if (blob) writeFileSync(`${dir}/${it.id}_${name}`, Buffer.from(await blob.arrayBuffer()));
  }
  delete it.image_path;
  delete it.cutout_path;
}
writeFileSync("datasets/pitch/demo_items.json", JSON.stringify(items, null, 1));
console.log(`${items.length} tagged items exported`);

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the images and data for the Fashion Aina product pitch (product-pitch/).

Run from experiments/pitch:  ../embeddings/.venv/bin/python -I build.py
Before it, once per refresh (both cached under datasets/pitch/, git-ignored):
  npx tsx --env-file=.env.local experiments/pitch/detect.ts       # the app's detector on demo_closet/
  node --env-file=.env.local experiments/pitch/export_demo.mjs    # the demo account's items: crops, cut-outs, tags
Writes product-pitch/assets/img/* (WebP), assets/fonts/*, assets/data.js. The page (index.html, style.css, app.js)
is hand-written and reads only data.js, so the folder can be copied anywhere (GitHub Pages) with no outside links.

Everything about the demo closet is the app pipeline's own output: boxes from detect.v1, crops/cut-outs/tags/colours
from the demo account (as the app stored them), silhouettes from the live matcher (head_v1, as match_one.py runs it).
"""
import json, re, shutil, sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageOps

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[1]
OUT = ROOT / "product-pitch"
IMG = OUT / "assets" / "img"
DS = ROOT / "datasets"
PITCH = DS / "pitch"
CLOSET = ROOT / "demo_closet"
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "experiments" / "silhouette-match"))

for d in ("photos", "garments", "cutouts"):  # regenerated every run, so nothing stale is left behind
    shutil.rmtree(IMG / d, ignore_errors=True)
for d in ("photos", "garments", "cutouts", "sil", "pairs", "colourpairs"):
    (IMG / d).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
(OUT / "assets" / "fonts").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
for f in (ROOT / "public" / "fonts").glob("cmu-serif-*.woff2"):
    shutil.copy(f, OUT / "assets" / "fonts" / f.name)


def save(im, path, max_h, q=82, max_w=None):
    im = im.copy()
    im.thumbnail((max_w or max_h * 3, max_h), Image.LANCZOS)
    im.save(path, "WEBP", quality=q, method=6)
    return {"w": im.width, "h": im.height}


def rel(p):
    return str(p.relative_to(OUT))


def slug(s):
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", s.lower()).strip("-")


LIB = json.load(open(ROOT / "src/lib/styling/silhouettes.json"))
LIB_BY = {s["id"]: s for s in LIB}


def sil_img(sid):
    """The library drawing on white with a margin all round, so no stroke touches the edge of its frame (cached)."""
    dst = IMG / "sil" / f"{sid}.webp"
    if not dst.exists():
        src = DS / "silhouettes" / "library" / f"{sid}_clean.png"
        if not src.exists():
            src = DS / "silhouettes" / "library" / f"{sid}.png"
        im = Image.open(src).convert("RGBA")
        white = Image.new("RGB", im.size, "white")
        white.paste(im, (0, 0), im)
        pad = int(0.07 * max(white.size))
        save(ImageOps.expand(white, border=pad, fill="white"), dst, 220, q=82)
    return rel(dst)


def cutout(src, dst):
    """A transparent cut-out, trimmed to the garment."""
    im = Image.open(src).convert("RGBA")
    bbox = im.getchannel("A").point(lambda v: 255 if v > 127 else 0).getbbox()
    save(im.crop(bbox) if bbox else im, dst, 320, q=84)
    return rel(dst)


data = {}

# ---- the live garment -> silhouette matcher (exactly as match_one.py runs it) ----------------------------------
from features import OUT as SM, Extractor  # noqa: E402
from train import IDS, SLOT, load_head  # noqa: E402

EX = Extractor()
HEAD = load_head(str(SM / "head_v1.npz"))


def match(cut_png, slot, k=3):
    im = Image.open(cut_png).convert("RGBA")
    mask = np.array(im)[:, :, 3] >= 128
    white = Image.new("RGB", im.size, (255, 255, 255))
    white.paste(im, (0, 0), im)
    idx = np.nonzero(SLOT == slot)[0]
    if not mask.any() or not len(idx):
        return []
    lg = HEAD.logits(EX.features([white], [mask])[0])[idx]
    p = np.exp(lg - lg.max())
    p /= p.sum()
    return [{"id": IDS[idx[i]], "name": LIB_BY[IDS[idx[i]]]["name"], "score": round(float(p[i]), 3),
             "img": sil_img(IDS[idx[i]])}

          <div class="decision">
            <b>Features that mean something.</b>
            Raw hex digits are a poor input &mdash; #a8 and #a9 are the same colour, #0f and #10 are far apart.
            Perceptual Lab lightness, hue and chroma beat hex and RGB at every depth, and a shallow shared encoder
            beat a 10-layer one.
          </div>
          <div class="decision">
            <b>Symmetric by construction, honest by measurement.</b>
            Both colours go through the same encoder, so A-with-B always equals B-with-A. Repeated pairs measure how

import re
p = "index.html"
s = open(p).read()
reps = [
    ("A second model, trained on the owner&rsquo;s ratings of drawn outfits,", "A second model, trained on hand-rated drawn outfits,"),
    ('id="matches-title">Matches from a model that never saw these garments</h3>', 'id="matches-title">The live matcher on the demo closet</h3>'),
    ("owner&rsquo;s ratings of drawn outfits.", "hand-rated drawn outfits."),
    ("<h3>What the owner rated</h3>", "<h3>What was rated</h3>"),
    ("Rank correlation with the owner&rsquo;s ratings on pairs, and on tops, held out of training.", "Rank correlation with the hand ratings on outfits, and on tops, held out of training."),
    ("Examples on this page come from the project&rsquo;s playground and test sets; numbers", "Examples on this page come from the demo closet, run through the app&rsquo;s own pipeline; numbers"),
    ("<b>Formality has a hard limit</b>Pieces more than one formality step apart never pair (two steps for accessories).", "<b>Formality has a hard limit</b>Pieces more than one formality step apart never pair."),
    ("<b>Seasons and necklines matter</b>No shared season costs 15%; a statement necklace on a high neckline is penalised.", "<b>Seasons matter</b>Two pieces with no season in common lose 15% of their score."),
]
for a, b in reps:
    assert a in s, a[:60]
    s = s.replace(a, b)
open(p, "w").write(s)
print("ok")

    ).join("");
    $("#thumbs").querySelectorAll("button").forEach((b) =>
      b.addEventListener("click", () => {
        state.photo = +b.dataset.i;
        state.garment = firstKept(PHOTOS[state.photo]);
        thumbs();
        viewer();
      }),
    );
  }

  function selectGarment(i) {
    state.garment = i;
    viewer();

python3 - <<'EOF'
p = "assets/app.js"
s = open(p).read()
a = s.index("  const MISS_NOTES = {")

a = s.index('    $("#matches-sub").textContent')
b = s.index("  function silPair() {")
new = '''    $("#matches-sub").textContent = `${D.matches.length} garments from the demo closet, as the app cut them out, with the live matcher's three closest silhouettes and its confidence in each. None of these garments was in the matcher's training data.`;
    $("#matches").innerHTML = D.matches
      .map(
        (m) => `<article class="match">
          <div>
            <div class="lightbox">${img(m.cutout, m.name)}</div>
            <div class="meta"><span class="badge">${esc(m.slot)}</span></div>
          </div>
          <div style="min-width:0">
            <div class="picks">${m.top
              .map(
                (t) => `<div class="pick" title="${esc(t.name)} · ${Math.round(t.score * 100)}%">
                  <div class="drawing">${img(t.img, t.name)}</div>
                  <div class="pct"><i style="width:${Math.max(3, t.score * 100)}%"></i></div>
                  <small>${esc(t.name)} · ${Math.round(t.score * 100)}%</small>
                </div>`,
              )
              .join("")}</div>
            <p class="label"><b>${esc(m.name)}</b></p>
          </div>
        </article>`,
      )
      .join("");
  }

'''
s = s[:a] + new + s[b:]
old_p = s[s.index("  const PRINCIPLES = ["):s.index("  ];", s.index("  const PRINCIPLES = ["))]
new_p = '''  const PRINCIPLES = [
    ["Judgement from rated examples, not hand-written rules", "Whether colours or shapes go together is learned from thousands of hand-rated pairs. A second rater can join with a learned offset and stretch, so different rating scales don't blur together."],
    ["Measure the ceiling before the model", "Every rating set mixes in repeats. A model is judged against how consistent the rater is: the shape model's error is 0.75 points, the rater's own is 0.68."],
    ["Synthetic to bootstrap, real to finish", "Renders of the drawings taught the matcher before any label existed; 671 real labels took it from 62% to 95.5% top-5."],
    ["Human in the loop where it's cheapest", "The user confirms garment boxes before anything is stored, and low-confidence tags are highlighted for review instead of trusted silently."],
    ["Cheap first, expensive only when unsure", "Rules score every pair instantly. The vision model only sees the uncertain middle band, in lists, under a budget."],
    ["Fixed vocabularies, validated outputs", "One taxonomy file, 121 named colours, schema-validated model output, versioned prompts. Nothing free-text reaches the scorer."],
    ["Fingerprints, not re-runs", "Each score records what it was computed from. Change a tag, retrain a model or edit a prompt, and exactly the affected pairs re-score."],
    ["Always a fallback", "An attribute bridge stands in before the matcher has run; the rule score stands when a vision call fails; a hand rule stands when a model has nothing to say."],
    ["Honest numbers", "Cross-validated scores and baselines beside every model; the garments on this page are the demo closet, run through the app's own pipeline."],
'''
s = s.replace(old_p, new_p)
open(p, "w").write(s)
print("ok")

`experiments/silhouette-pairs/train.py` on 495 ratings (450 distinct pairs, 45 repeats). Per silhouette the input is measured, never a name:
outline profile (24), 7 shape scalars, 12 PCA components of the drawn-detail grid, attribute multi-hot, button/pocket counts. Ordered-pair net:
head([e_t, e_b, e_t*e_b, |e_t-e_b|]) over two slot towers, ensemble of 3. Held-out MAE/Spearman - unseen pairs 0.79/0.48, unseen tops 0.85/0.43,
unseen bottoms 0.83/0.43; rater test-retest MAE 0.64 is the floor. Beats mean-by-top + mean-by-bottom, so the interaction is real, but it is
0.15 above the rater, so the lookup table stays and the model only fills unrated pairs. Rounds append to `datasets/silhouettepairs/train_log.jsonl`.
Not done: feature ablations (does the attribute block earn its place?), weight export to TypeScript.

## Dark-only UI with light boxes; cutouts always (2026-10-23)
User asked for a dark wardrobe feel with "light boxes" around garments, no room furniture or floor texture.
- `globals.css` is dark only (`color-scheme: dark`, no `prefers-color-scheme` branch): warm near-black, plum accent, plus a warm bulb
  (`--light`, `--glow`). `.lightbox` is a softly lit panel (radial glow brighter than the page, 2px strip light on the top edge, glow on hover);
  `.lightbox-img` shows the garment with `object-contain` and its own drop shadow. The panel interior is deliberately LIGHTER than the page so a
  black garment still has an edge; `object-cover` was dropped because cutouts must not be cropped.
- Background removal is no longer opt-in: `uploadOne(..., { removeBg: true })` for every photo (`@imgly/background-removal`, in-browser, falls
  back to the plain photo on failure). `listItems` already prefers `cutout_path`.
- Several garments in one photo: the user drags a box around each (`src/components/garment-splitter.tsx`), each box is cropped
  (`cropToFile`, geometry in the pure `src/lib/upload/crop.ts`) and goes through the normal upload path, so each item gets its own cutout and tags.
  Chosen over automatic instance segmentation (no model for it; the tagger does not return boxes) as the simplest thing that works; auto-detection
  can replace the drawing step later without changing the pipeline.
Not verified visually: no browser in this session and the signed-in pages need a Supabase project.

## Detect-then-choose upload (detect.v1)
Every photo now goes through a review step before anything is stored: a vision call (`/api/items/detect`, `detect.v1`,
model `MODEL_DETECT` or `MODEL_TAGGER`, logged as purpose `detect`) returns one box and a label per garment; all boxes start
ticked, the user unticks what they do not want, can drag extra boxes, or adds the whole photo, then only the ticked boxes are
cropped, cut out, uploaded and tagged. Chosen from the three options in `docs/EXTRA-FEATURES.md` #1: the vision call handles any

  const pendingTag = all.filter((i) => i.slot === UNTAGGED && !i.rejection_reason);
  const needsDetails = all.filter(

        i.garment_detail === null ||

@import "tailwindcss";

/* One small design system, dark only: near-black with a purple cast, and three pop colours (purple, pink, blue) used
   as a gradient. Type is Computer Modern (CMU Serif), self-hosted. Palette and the eyebrow/statement heading pattern
   are taken from stylebuddy.fashion, which the user gave as the design reference.
   Garments are shown as background-free cutouts inside a "light box": a lit panel that makes a garment of any colour
   read against the dark page. Every animation is wrapped so that it does not run for someone who asked for less
   motion. */

}

}

/* ---- motion ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
@keyframes rise {
  from {

}

"use client";

import { useRouter } from "next/navigation";
import { useState } from "react";
import { runPool, tagItem } from "@/lib/upload/pipeline";

/** Retries tagging for items that were uploaded but never tagged (e.g. a failed or limited run). */
export function TagUntagged({
  ids,
  kind = "untagged",
}: {
  ids: string[];
  kind?: "untagged" | "details";
}) {
  const router = useRouter();
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const [errors, setErrors] = useState<string[]>([]);

  async function run() {
    setBusy(true);
    setErrors([]);
    const errs: string[] = [];
    await runPool(ids, 3, async (id) => {
      try {
        await tagItem(id);
      } catch (e) {
        errs.push(e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Tagging failed");
      }
    });
    setErrors([...new Set(errs)]);
    setBusy(false);
    router.refresh();
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-1 rounded-lg border border-amber-400 p-3 text-sm">
      <p>
        {kind === "details"
          ? `${ids.length} garment${ids.length === 1 ? " needs" : "s need"} fit and length tags for better matching.`
          : `${ids.length} item${ids.length === 1 ? "" : "s"} not tagged yet.`}
      </p>
      <button
        onClick={run}
        disabled={busy}
        className="self-start rounded-lg border border-[var(--line)] px-3 py-1 disabled:opacity-50"
      >
        {busy ? "Tagging…" : kind === "details" ? "Add fit & length" : "Tag now"}
      </button>
      {errors.map((e) => (
        <p key={e} role="alert" className="text-red-400">
          {e}
        </p>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
"use client";

import { useRouter } from "next/navigation";
import { useState } from "react";
import { LiveRefresh } from "@/components/live-refresh";

/** Queues background (re)scoring of all pairs, e.g. for items tagged before pair scoring existed. */
export function RescoreButton() {
  const router = useRouter();
  const [state, setState] = useState<"idle" | "queued" | "error">("idle");
  async function run() {
    const res = await fetch("/api/pairs/refresh", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
      body: "{}",
    });
    setState(res.ok ? "queued" : "error");
    if (res.ok) setTimeout(() => setState("idle"), 120_000); // keep polling for 2 minutes
    router.refresh();
  }
  return (
    <div className="text-sm">
      <LiveRefresh active={state === "queued"} />
      <button onClick={run} className="rounded-lg border border-[var(--line)] px-3 py-1">
        Re-score all pairs
      </button>
      {state === "queued" && (
        <span className="ml-2 muted">
          Scoring in the background; results appear as they finish.
        </span>
      )}
      {state === "error" && <span className="ml-2 text-red-400">Could not start scoring.</span>}
    </div>
  );
}

      ? "border border-[var(--accent)] text-[var(--accent)]"
      : "border border-[var(--line)] muted";

/** The whole journey of a photo, with the current step lit: find, choose, cut out, upload, tag, score. */
export function PipelineSteps({ current }: { current: number }) {
  return (
    <ol aria-label="Steps" className="flex flex-wrap gap-1 text-[11px]">
      {PIPELINE_STEPS.map((label, i) => (
        <li
          key={label}
          aria-current={i === current ? "step" : undefined}
          className={`rounded-full px-2 py-0.5 ${pill(i < current ? "done" : i === current ? "active" : "todo")}`}
        >
          {i + 1}. {label}
        </li>
      ))}
    </ol>
  );
}

  const pct = jobs.length ? Math.round(((done + failed) / jobs.length) * 100) : 0;

  const review = photos.find((x) => x.phase === "ready");
  const finding = photos.filter((x) => x.phase === "finding");
  const waiting = photos.filter((x) => x.phase === "ready").length;

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
      {review && (
        <div
          role="dialog"
          aria-modal="true"
          aria-label="Choose what to add"
          className="fixed inset-0 z-50 overflow-y-auto bg-black/70 p-4"
        >
          <div className="mx-auto max-w-md rounded-xl border border-[var(--line)] bg-[var(--bg)] p-4">
            {waiting + finding.length > 1 && (
              <p className="muted mb-2 text-sm">
                {waiting + finding.length - 1} more photo{waiting + finding.length === 2 ? "" : "s"}{" "}
                after this one
              </p>
            )}
            <GarmentSplitter
              key={review.key}
              file={review.file}
              found={review.found}
              note={review.note}
              onCancel={() => setPhotos((prev) => prev.filter((x) => x.key !== review.key))}
              onConfirm={(boxes, whole) => void splitInto(review, boxes, whole)}
            />
          </div>
        </div>
      )}
      <div className="flex gap-2">
        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={() => cameraRef.current?.click()}
          className="btn btn-primary flex-1"
        >
          Take photo
        </button>
        <button type="button" onClick={() => galleryRef.current?.click()} className="btn flex-1">
          Choose photos
        </button>
      </div>
      <input
        ref={cameraRef}
        type="file"
        accept="image/*"
        capture="environment"
        hidden
        onChange={(e) => {
          start(e.target.files);
          e.target.value = "";
        }}
      />
      <input
        ref={galleryRef}
        type="file"
        accept="image/*,.heic,.heif"
        multiple
        hidden
        onChange={(e) => {
          start(e.target.files);
          e.target.value = "";
        }}
      />

      <p className="muted text-sm">
        Every photo is checked for garments first and you choose which to keep. Backgrounds are then

/* ---- shared pieces used across the signed-in pages ---------------------------------------------------------- */
@layer components {
  /* page title block: eyebrow, title, one line of context */
  .page-head {
    display: flex;

    gap: 0.25rem;
  }
  .page-title {
    font-size: 1.9rem;
    font-weight: 600;
    line-height: 1.15;
  }

    gap: 0.25rem;
    min-height: 2.25rem;
    font-size: 0.9rem;
    color: var(--muted);
    transition: color 0.15s;
  }
  .back:hover {
    color: var(--foreground);
  }

  /* inline messages: a tinted panel with a coloured edge, readable on the dark page */
  .notice {
    --tone: var(--light);
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    gap: 0.5rem;
    border-radius: 0.9rem;
    border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--tone) 45%, transparent);
    background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--tone) 10%, var(--surface));
    padding: 0.8rem 1rem;
    font-size: 0.9rem;
    line-height: 1.4;
  }
  .notice-warn {
    --tone: var(--warn);
  }
  .notice-danger {
    --tone: var(--danger);
  }
  .notice a {
    text-decoration: underline;
    text-underline-offset: 3px;
  }
  .text-warn {
    color: var(--warn);
  }
  .text-danger {
    color: var(--danger);
  }

  .btn-sm {

  }
  .btn-danger:hover {
    border-color: var(--danger);

  }

  const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState("");

  const set = <K extends keyof EditableTags>(k: K, v: EditableTags[K]) =>
    setDraft((d) => ({ ...d, [k]: v }));
  const low = (k: string) => (item.tag_confidence?.[k] ?? 1) < LOW_CONFIDENCE;
  const hl = (k: string) => (low(k) ? "ring-2 ring-amber-400" : "");
  const isJewellery = draft.slot?.startsWith("jewellery");
  const hasNeckline = draft.slot === "top" || draft.slot === "dress" || draft.slot === "onepiece";

  async function call(method: "PATCH" | "DELETE", body?: unknown) {
    setSaving(true);
    setError("");
    const res = await fetch(`/api/items/${item.id}`, {
      method,
      headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
      body: body ? JSON.stringify(body) : undefined,
    });
    const json = await res.json().catch(() => null);
    setSaving(false);
    if (!json?.ok) return setError(json?.error ?? "Save failed");
    return true;

import Link from "next/link";
import { createClient } from "@/lib/supabase/server";
import { WARDROBE_BUCKET } from "@/lib/storage-paths";
import { UNTAGGED } from "@/lib/styling/taxonomy";
import { ReviewCarousel, type ReviewItem } from "./carousel";

export default async function ReviewPage({
  searchParams,
}: {
  searchParams: Promise<{ item?: string }>;
}) {
  const { item: focusId } = await searchParams;
  const supabase = await createClient();
  const { data } = await supabase
    .from("items")
    .select(
      "id, slot, category, subcategory, colors, pattern, fabric, formality, warmth, seasons, neckline, statement_level, metal_tone, style_tags, occasions, tag_confidence, tags_confirmed, rejection_reason, image_path, cutout_path, thumb_path",
    )
    .eq("archived", false)
    .order("created_at", { ascending: true });

  // Needs a look: unconfirmed AI tags, plus rejected photos waiting for manual tags.
  const rows = (data ?? [])
    .filter((r) =>
      r.slot === UNTAGGED ? !!r.rejection_reason || r.id === focusId : !r.tags_confirmed,
    )
    .sort((a, b) => Number(b.id === focusId) - Number(a.id === focusId));
  const pathOf = (r: (typeof rows)[number]) => r.cutout_path ?? r.image_path;
  const { data: signed } = rows.length
    ? await supabase.storage.from(WARDROBE_BUCKET).createSignedUrls(rows.map(pathOf), 3600)
    : { data: [] };
  const urlByPath = new Map((signed ?? []).map((s) => [s.path, s.signedUrl]));
  const items: ReviewItem[] = rows.map((r) => ({
    ...(r as unknown as ReviewItem),
    image_url: urlByPath.get(pathOf(r)) ?? null,
  }));

  return (
    <main className="mx-auto flex min-h-dvh max-w-md flex-col gap-4 p-4">
      <Link href="/closet" className="text-sm muted">
        ← Closet
      </Link>
      <h1 className="text-2xl font-semibold">Review tags</h1>
      {items.length === 0 ? (
        <p className="py-16 text-center muted">Everything is reviewed. 🎉</p>
      ) : (
        <ReviewCarousel items={items} />
      )}
    </main>
  );
}

# UI notes (branch `ui-design`)

Kept apart from `DECISIONS.md` so this branch and the backend branch do not edit the same file; fold in at merge time.

## Pass 1: one set of shared pieces (2026-10-24)
- Status colours are three tokens in `globals.css` (`--warn`, `--danger`, `--ok`), used through `.notice[-warn|-danger]`, `.badge`, `.text-warn`, `.text-danger`. No raw Tailwind palette classes (`amber-*`, `red-*`) in pages any more.
- New components: `PageHeader` (back link, eyebrow, title, one line of context) and `Notice`. Every signed-in page uses `PageHeader`.
- New classes: `.btn-sm`, `.btn-danger`, `.field-sm` / `.field-flag` (review screen), `.chip`, `.progress`, `.sheet` (upload modal), `.meter` (match strength under a score), `.rail` (pill row that scrolls to the screen edge), `.tabbar` / `.tab` (bottom nav with a lit active edge, safe-area padding).
- Fixed: the upload modal used `var(--bg)`, which does not exist (transparent panel); the review screen used light amber notes on the dark page; the review photo is now in a light box like everywhere else.
- Style pages show the match as a bar as well as a number. Pills get a bigger touch target on coarse pointers.
- `/preview` shows every new piece (needs `TAGGER_PLAYGROUND=1`). Signed-in pages were not rendered in a browser (they need Supabase and a login); they were checked by typecheck, lint, tests and the shared classes on `/preview`.

## Scope rule while two branches are open
UI work touches `src/app/**` pages, `src/components/**`, `globals.css`, `public/` and this file only. Nothing in `src/lib`, `datasets`, `experiments`, `evals` or `DECISIONS.md`.
EOF

Turn 163

what is the input for the silhuette-silhouette-compatibility rating? is it just silhouette names or silhouette features ?
Claude's response

It's silhouette features, not names. The rated pairs also feed a lookup table keyed by silhouette, so the names do get used, just not as model input.

This comes from the pair-model entry in DECISIONS.md. I haven't re-checked experiments/silhouette-pairs/train.py itself.

What the model sees for each silhouette ("measured, never a name") - An outline profile of 24 numbers. - 7 shape scalars. - 12 PCA components of the 24×16 drawn-detail grid. - A multi-hot vector of the hand-recorded attributes: fit, length, neckline, collar, sleeves, closure, pockets, construction, hem, and for bottoms rise, leg shape and waistband. - The button and pocket counts.

How a pair is scored - Each side goes through its own tower, one for tops and one for bottoms, giving embeddings e_t and e_b. - The head takes [e_t, e_b, e_t*e_b, |e_t-e_b|], a 3-model ensemble. - The order is fixed (top, then bottom). The model is not symmetric.

Where names still appear - Your ratings are stored against silhouette names or ids, and that table is used as a lookup for pairs you've actually rated. - The model only fills in pairs you haven't rated. It scores 0.79 MAE on unseen pairs, against 0.64 for your own test-retest, so the table stays for now. - Because the model takes features, a new silhouette needs only its features, not new training data for its name.

I answered from the notes rather than a plan, since nothing needs implementing, so I haven't written a plan file or changed anything. If you want me to check train.py and the TypeScript side, say so and I'll read them. Both are read-only.

The pair model's features are read by one Python function, silhouette_features() in experiments/silhouette-pairs/train.py:43. No app code reads them yet.

What silhouette_features() does - It loads src/lib/styling/silhouettes.json and silhouette-vocab.json. - For each silhouette it takes the stored 24-number profile and the shape scalars. - It takes a 12-component PCA of the drawn-detail grid, computed at load time with an SVD of the grid matrix (pca = g @ vt[:12].T). - It builds the attribute multi-hot from the vocabulary lists. - It adds the button count divided by 10 and the pocket count divided by 4. - It concatenates all of that into one vector per silhouette id, tagged with the slot (top or bottom). - tower_dims, fit_mlp and the other training code then use those vectors.

Where the features come from - The profile, scalars and detail grid are measured from the drawings by experiments/silhouettes/ingest.py. - The attributes are hand-recorded, validated by attr/build.py, and merged into silhouettes.json by ingest.py.

On the TypeScript side - src/lib/styling/silhouettes.ts only loads the same JSON and exposes SILHOUETTES, silhouetteById, silhouettesForSlot and a Zod schema. - The only importer I found is tests/silhouettes.test.ts, so no app code consumes the features. - The notes say the weight export to TypeScript isn't done, so the app can't score silhouette pairs yet. - The separate experiments/silhouette-match/ code, which matches a garment photo to a silhouette, has its own features.py. Yes, it's doable. I'd build it as a personal layer on top of the shared models, not by retraining the shared models from each user's stars.

What's already in place (read-only check) - The colour-pair model is a small network whose weights are a JSON file (colour-pair-model.json), evaluated in TypeScript in colourPair.ts. It uses 6 numbers per colour (Lab lightness, a, b, chroma, hue). - pairScore.ts blends the colour score with the other parts and weights them. - The schema already has feedback_events and style_profiles tables, so there's somewhere to store taste. - Pair scores carry a fingerprint, so stored pairs re-score when a weight changes. Personal weights would go into that fingerprint.

How I'd do it 1. Star storage. Save each star, and also what was shown and not starred, as weak negatives. Stars alone only say "liked", so I'd add a "not for me" action too. 2. Personal layer. Per user, fit a small regularised model (ridge or logistic) on the same features the shared models use. That's colour features for the colour part, and silhouette feature vectors or embeddings for the silhouette part. It predicts a correction to the shared score, not a replacement. 3. Blend weight. The weight starts at zero and grows with the number of stars. With 5 stars the shared models still decide, and by about 50 the user's taste is visible. This is the "gradually" you asked for. 4. Refit. This is cheap, a few dozen to a few hundred rows. It can run in the browser or on the server after each star, with no GPU.

Why not retrain the shared nets per user - A user will give tens of signals against the 495 ratings the shared silhouette model trained on. Fine-tuning would overfit, and storing per-user weights is heavy. - The rater's own test-retest is MAE 0.64, so one person's labels are noisy. A heavily regularised residual copes with that better.

Problems to settle first - The silhouette model isn't in TypeScript yet. The notes say the weight export isn't done, and no app code reads silhouette features today. The silhouette half of this needs that export first. The colour half can start now. - Credit assignment. A starred outfit is a whole look. Did they like the colour pair or the shapes? With few stars, one star updates both layers, which blurs the signal. I'd update on features that differ from what the shared models already predict. - Silhouette identification. The silhouette side depends on the planned tagger v12 that identifies a garment's silhouette from a photo. Until then it has no input from real garments. - Position bias. Users star what's shown first. Showing a few lower-ranked picks occasionally gives honest negatives. - Privacy. The stars are the user's own data, so they'd sit behind the existing per-user row-level security rules. I'd check that rather than assume it.

How I'd check it works. Hold out some of a user's stars and measure whether the personalised ranking puts them higher than the shared one does. For a demo, simulate users with fixed tastes (say, someone who prefers high contrast) and check that the layer learns that.

This question ended up as a plan-mode turn, so I made no changes. If you want it written up as a staged plan, say so. I'd order it as the star UI and storage first, then the colour personal layer, then the silhouette layer once its export lands.

# Indian wear: pipeline proposal

## Context
The app's taxonomy already knows some Indian wear: `kurti` (top), `palazzo` (bottom), `saree` / `lehenga` / `anarkali` / `salwar_set` / `kurta_set` (slot `onepiece`, "Ethnic sets"), `dupatta_shawl` (outerwear) and `mojari_juttis` (shoes). `pattern_detail` already has ikat, bandhani, block print, brocade, zari and mirror work. The tagger (`tagger.v11`) has rules for kurta vs kurta set.

But the styling side is Western only:
- Sets are stored as one `onepiece` item, so they can't be mixed and matched.
- The 165 silhouettes in the library are Western tops and bottoms.
- The pair models rate two pieces, but Indian outfits are often three: kurta + bottom + dupatta, saree + blouse, or lehenga + choli + dupatta.

The goal is for Indian wear to go through the same pipeline as Western wear: detect → tag → identify silhouette → score pairs/outfits → show.

This is mostly backend work, which the other session owns. It belongs in the roadmap ("Later: kurta, salwar, coats…"), not on the `ui-design` branch. The UI part is stage 8.

# Extending the closet: Indian clothes + a fuller Western wardrobe

## Context
The user wants two additions to the closet, both before the jewellery pass:
- Indian clothes.
- More Western garment types: jackets, sweaters and other missing types.

**Assumption (from the user):** people are asked for clear photos, one garment per photo or pieces laid apart with no overlap. That removes the hard segmentation work, so stage 1 only needs new labels.

**Where things stand:**
- The taxonomy already has some categories: `kurti`, `palazzo`, `sweater` (as a top), `jacket` / `blazer` / `cardigan` / `coat` / `shrug` / `dupatta_shawl` (outerwear), and sets as one `onepiece` item (`saree`, `lehenga`, `anarkali`, `salwar_set`, `kurta_set`).
- The silhouette library is only Western tops and bottoms: 220 silhouettes (103 tops, 117 bottoms) across tees, tops, shirts, pants, shorts and skirts.
- There are no silhouettes for kurtas, ethnic bottoms, sweaters, outerwear or dresses.
- The pair models score only top × bottom.

This is mostly backend work, so it goes to the other session or a later pass. Stage 7 includes the UI part for this branch.

## Garment types to add

**Indian (stored as separate pieces, not as one set item):**

| Slot | New categories |
|---|---|
| top | `kurta` (long; `kurti` stays for short), `blouse_saree`, `choli` |
| bottom | `salwar`, `churidar`, `sharara`, `gharara`, `patiala`, `dhoti_pants`, `lehenga_skirt` (`palazzo` exists) |
| drape (new slot) | `dupatta`, `stole` (moved out of outerwear) |
| onepiece | `saree`, `anarkali` (true one-piece garments only) |

Sets (`salwar_set`, `kurta_set`, `lehenga`, `co_ord_set`) become pieces linked by a `set_id`. The user photographs each piece separately and ticks "same set" on the review screen.

**Western, to complete the closet:**

| Slot | Add | Why |
|---|---|---|
| top | `hoodie`, `sweatshirt`, `turtleneck`, `polo`, `camisole`, `bodysuit` | everyday basics that are missing |
| knitwear | `sweater` stays a top; add `cardigan` here as well | sweaters are worn alone, cardigans as layers |
| outerwear | `denim_jacket`, `leather_jacket`, `bomber`, `trench`, `puffer`, `overshirt`, `vest_gilet`, `waistcoat` | "jacket" is too broad to style with |
| bottom | `cargo`, `joggers`, `skort` | common bottoms with their own look |
| dress | `shirt_dress`, `wrap_dress`, `slip_dress`, `bodycon`, `sundress`, `playsuit` | dress shape drives what goes over it |

I left out wide-leg, flared and similar shapes on purpose. Those are silhouettes (stage 4), not categories.

Here's what adding Indian wear (no jewellery yet) takes, stage by stage. It assumes clear photos with one piece per photo, a flat or folded saree, and each piece of a set photographed separately.

# Stage What gets added What you have to do
1 Segmentation detect.v2 with the new labels only (kurta, salwar, churidar, sharara, gharara, dupatta, saree, blouse, choli, lehenga skirt). No overlap handling, since photos are clear. Upload tips ask for one piece per photo. Take about 20 clear test photos of Indian pieces. They're the eval set for stages 1, 2 and 4.
2 Tagging New categories in taxonomy.ts. Sets become separate pieces joined by a set_id. A new drape slot holds the dupatta. tagger.v12 adds kurta length and cut, Indian necklines, ethnic leg shapes, work techniques (chikankari, gota, zardozi…), fabrics (silk, Banarasi, chanderi…), saree border and pallu, and dupatta weight. A migration adds the new columns. Check the tagger's answers on the 20 photos (the playground review UI), as you did for v11. Decide whether festive should split into wedding and puja.
3 Colour picker + colour-pair model Add any missing jewel tones (rani pink, mustard, peacock, bottle green, maroon) to colours.json and rebuild. The model itself stays as it is. Rate a short extra batch of colour pairs in those tones in the labeler.
4 Garment → silhouette matcher + silhouette-pair model Kurta and ethnic-bottom silhouettes go through the existing ingest.py → attributes → silhouettes.json. Retrain the matcher. Add a kurta × bottom labeler template and retrain the pair model. The biggest part. Supply line-drawing sheets of kurta cuts and ethnic bottoms. Rate a few hundred kurta × bottom pairs, chosen by active learning.
5 pairScore Three-piece outfits: kurta + bottom + optional dupatta, saree + blouse, lehenga skirt + choli + dupatta. Colour is summed over the pairs and weighted by area. Add a one-heavy-print rule, and a bonus for keeping a set together that still allows splitting it. Rate a small set of three-piece outfits to check the score.
6 Vision ranker A rank.v4 prompt that knows the Indian outfit templates and fusion looks (kurta + jeans, saree + shirt). Spot-check its picks.
7 Matches slots.ts and matches.ts build the three-piece outfits. On the UI branch: an Ethnic filter, set grouping, outfit cards with three pieces, and new review fields plus a "same set" tick. Try it end to end: upload a kurta, salwar and dupatta as one set and check what Style suggests.

Your part in short: the test photos, the silhouette sheets, and the pair ratings. Stage 4 is most of the effort.

Most of this is backend work, so it fits the other session or a later pass. Only the stage 7 UI belongs on this branch. Jackets, sweaters and the other Western types can follow the same table when you're ready.

7	type Ctx = { params: Promise<{ id: string }> };

9	/** Saves user edits to tags, marks them confirmed, and logs a tag_correction per changed field. */
10	export async function PATCH(req: NextRequest, { params }: Ctx) {
11	  const auth = await requireUser();
12	  if ("response" in auth) return auth.response;
13	  const { id } = await params;
14	  const parsed = PatchItemRequest.safeParse(await req.json().catch(() => null));
15	  if (!parsed.success) return zodFail(parsed.error);
16	  const { confirm, ...edits } = parsed.data;
17	
18	  const { data: current } = await auth.supabase
19	    .from("items")
20	    .select("*")
21	    .eq("id", id)
22	    .maybeSingle();
23	  if (!current) return fail("Item not found", 404);
24	
25	  const slot = edits.slot ?? current.slot;
26	  const category = edits.category ?? current.category;
27	  if (!categoryMatchesSlot(slot, category))
28	    return fail("Category does not belong to that slot", 422);
29	
30	  const changed = Object.entries(edits).filter(
31	    ([k, v]) => JSON.stringify(v) !== JSON.stringify(current[k]),
32	  );
33	  const { error } = await auth.supabase
34	    .from("items")
35	    .update({
36	      ...edits,
37	      ...(confirm ? { tags_confirmed: true } : {}),
38	      // manually tagging a previously rejected photo resolves the rejection
39	      ...(edits.slot ? { rejection_reason: null } : {}),
40	    })
41	    .eq("id", id);
42	  if (error) return fail(error.message, 500);
43	
44	  if (changed.length) {
45	    await auth.supabase.from("feedback_events").insert(
46	      changed.map(([field, to]) => ({
47	        user_id: auth.user.id,
48	        item_id: id,
49	        type: "tag_correction",
50	        payload: { field, from: current[field], to, tagger_version: current.tagger_version },
51	      })),
52	    );
53	  }
54	  if (changed.length) {
55	    const userId = auth.user.id;
56	    after(() => refreshPairsForItem(userId, id).catch(() => undefined));
57	  }
58	  return ok({ changed: changed.map(([k]) => k) });
59	}
60	
61	export async function DELETE(_req: NextRequest, { params }: Ctx) {
62	  const auth = await requireUser();
63	  if ("response" in auth) return auth.response;
64	  const { id } = await params;
65	  const { data: item } = await auth.supabase
66	    .from("items")
67	    .select("image_path, cutout_path, thumb_path")
68	    .eq("id", id)
69	    .maybeSingle();
70	  if (!item) return fail("Item not found", 404);
71	  const paths = [item.image_path, item.cutout_path, item.thumb_path].filter(
72	    (p): p is string => !!p,
73	  );
74	  await auth.supabase.storage.from(WARDROBE_BUCKET).remove(paths);
75	  const { error } = await auth.supabase.from("items").delete().eq("id", id);
76	  if (error) return fail(error.message, 500);
77	  return ok({ deleted: true });
78	}

15	      body: "{}",
16	    });
17	    setState(res.ok ? "queued" : "error");

19	    router.refresh();
20	  }
21	  return (
22	    <div className="text-sm">

# Add "remove from closet" on the item detail page

## Context
The closet view (`/closet`) lists items as cards that link to either `/closet/review?item=…`
(untagged items) or `/style/[itemId]` (tagged items). There is currently no way for a user to
delete an item from the main closet flow — the only existing delete UI lives in the review
carousel (`src/app/(app)/closet/review/carousel.tsx`), which is reached only for untagged items.
Tagged items that a user wants to get rid of have no path to deletion at all.

The backend already supports deletion fully: `DELETE /api/items/[id]`
(`src/app/api/items/[id]/route.ts:61-78`) removes the storage objects (`image_path`,
`cutout_path`, `thumb_path`) from `WARDROBE_BUCKET` and deletes the `items` row.

Per the user's choice, we leave closet-list click/navigation behavior untouched and instead add a
"Remove from closet" action to the item detail page (`src/app/(app)/style/[itemId]/page.tsx`),
which is where a click on any tagged closet item already lands.

## Approach
1. **New client component** `src/components/remove-item-button.tsx`:
   - `"use client"`, modeled on the existing `RescoreButton`
     (`src/components/rescore-button.tsx`) and the carousel's `call()` + `confirm()` pattern
     (`src/app/(app)/closet/review/carousel.tsx:150-162`).
   - Props: `{ itemId: string }`.
   - On click: `confirm("Remove this item from your closet? This can't be undone.")` → if

"use client";

import { useRouter } from "next/navigation";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Trash2 } from "lucide-react";

/** Deletes the item (storage files + row) and sends the user back to the closet. */
export function RemoveItemButton({ itemId }: { itemId: string }) {
  const router = useRouter();
  const [deleting, setDeleting] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState("");

  async function remove() {
    if (!confirm("Remove this item from your closet? This can't be undone.")) return;
    setDeleting(true);
    setError("");
    const res = await fetch(`/api/items/${itemId}`, { method: "DELETE" });
    const json = await res.json().catch(() => null);
    if (!json?.ok) {
      setDeleting(false);
      setError(json?.error ?? "Could not remove item");
      return;
    }
    router.push("/closet");
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-1">
      <button
        onClick={remove}
        disabled={deleting}
        className="muted inline-flex items-center gap-1 text-sm text-red-400 underline underline-offset-4 disabled:opacity-60"
      >
        <Trash2 size={14} aria-hidden="true" />
        {deleting ? "Removing…" : "Remove from closet"}
      </button>
      {error && <span className="text-xs text-red-400">{error}</span>}
    </div>
  );
}
